begin(abstract) quantifying the complexity of quantum states that possess intrinsic structure such as symmetry or encoding in a fair manner constitutes a core challenge in the benchmarking of quantum technologies . this paper introduces the referencontingent complexity rcc an informatioheoretic measure calibrated by the available quantum operations . the core idea is to leverage the quantum relative entropy to quantify the deviation of a quantum state from its structured vacuum—namely the maximum entropy state within its constrained subspace—thereby only pricing the process of creating norivial information . our central result is a key theorem that rigorously proves the rcc serves as a lower bound for the complexity of any universal quantum circuit . this lower bound is comprised of a linear dominant term a universal logarithmic correction and a precise physical correction term that accounts for noniformity in the spectral distribution . crucially we establish a set of operational protocols grounded in tasks like quantum hypothesis testing which make this theoretical lower bound experimentally auditable . this work provides a ruler for quantum technology that is structurair and enables croslatform comparison thereby establishing a strictly verifiable constraint between the computational cost of the process and the structured information of the final state . end(abstract) keywords(quantum circuit complexity structural fairness quantum benchmarking singlhot quantum information theory relative entropy kolmogorov complexity) section(introduction) what precisely might constitute the intrinsic complexity of a manody quantum state ? driven by quantum information science this fundamental question is increasingly becoming a bridge connecting computational theory and fundamental physics profoundly influencing our understanding of the potential of quantum computation the black hole information paradox and its later developments the emergence of spacetime geometry and even phases of matter . at the core of answering this question lies the quantification of the minimum computational resources required to prepare a specific quantum state . this perspective is not only key to assessing the potential of quantum algorithms but also provides a fundamental benchmark for measuring the true performance of quantum hardware with concrete diagnostics developed in recent works . although various profound paradigms for complexity measures have been developed in the field—including nielsens complexity based on geometric shortest paths krylov complexity based on operator algebra growth and resource theories closely related to quantum computational advantage e.g . magitate and related approaches recent links to operator growth and general resourcheoretic formalisms —a lontanding challenge remains to be systematically addressed how to conduct a fair complexity accounting for a structured quantum system . the salled structural fairness problem originates from the ubiquitous presence of encodings and symmetries in quantum information processing which can dramatically reshape what should count as a genuine computational cost . taking a faulolerant quantum computer as an example its information is encoded within a certain code subspace of a vast physical hilbert space ; for a basic operation executed on a logical qubit its true computational cost should depend on the change in the logical information rather than the apparent consumption of mobilizing many physical qubits to maintain the erroorrecting code structure . in practice logical operations may be realized via nontrivial transformations supported by the code architecture itself . if a complexity measure cannot distinguish between these two it could lead to the misleading conclusion that the larger the physical scale of the system and the more complex the encoding structure the higher its complexity is assessed to be . similarly in symmetrrotected topological spt phases or strongly correlated systems the lonergy physics is confined to specific symmetry sectors ; a fair measure ought to treat these structures—endowed for free by the hamiltonians symmetries—as an a priori background and only measure the cost of generating norivial quantum correlations on top of this background . this viewpoint is consistent with broader perspectives on emergent phases and constrained dynamics . existing frameworks for measures often find it difficult to systematically isolate these free structures leading to a lack of a unified and fair benchmark when making crosomparisons of complexity across different physical systems or encoding schemes . to directly address this challenge this paper establishes a theory for quantum complexity lower bounds that is structurally fair theoretically rigorous and operationally accessible . its core is the introduction and systematic construction of the theoretical framework of referencontingent complexity rcc and its core contributions can be summarized into the following three points begin(enumerate) item establishing a structurally fair complexity benchmark we start from first principles and introduce the mathematical construct of a reference set to formalize any given physical structure whether originating from symmetries or encoding schemes as an a priori background . we then define complexity as the informatioheoretic distance of a quantum state relative to this background represented by the maximuntropy reference state namely the quantum relative entropy . this construction fundamentally ensures that our proposed measure rcc only prices the norivial information that transcends the a priori structure thereby addressing the structural fairness problem . item proving it as a theoreevel lower bound for universal circuit complexity we prove a central theorem establishing that rcc is a rigorous lower bound on the complexity of any universal quantum circuit . this lower bound is dominated by a linear leading term supplemented by a universal logarithmic correction and includes a physical correction term with a coefficient of exactly which characterizes the spectral distribution of the quantum state . this result establishes a quantitative link between the physical cost of the computational process and the informatioheoretic properties of the final state . item connecting the theory with operational observables to connect this theoretical lower bound with physical reality we construct a set of operational protocols based on schemes such as quantum hypothesis testing . these protocols transform an abstract theoretical concept into a set of physical observables that can be estimated experimentally with statistical confidence providing a practical theoretical tool for complexity benchmarking in real quantum systems . end(enumerate) the structure of this paper is organized as follows . we first systematically establish the theoretical framework for referencontingent complexity rcc in sec . and then proceed in sec . to propose and prove the central theorem of its role as a strict lower bound for circuit complexity . to connect this theory with physical reality sec . delves into the operational principles of rcc . building on this foundation sec . presents the axiomatic properties of rcc and its three major application interfaces while sec . discusses it within a broader theoretical context . sec . provides a summary of the entire paper . to ensure the selonsistency of the manuscript and the completeness of the arguments all technical derivations are systematically organized in the appendices . among them the core theoretical cornerstones—the rigorous proof of the main theorem the robustness of the framework and the operational protocols—are elaborated in detail in appendices and respectively . building upon this we further extend the boundaries of the theory appendices and explore the connections of this framework with other theories and its generalization to broader settings while appendix provides constructive evidence for the central conjecture in the main text . finally to support the key application interfaces in the main text appendix provides a complete technical supplement on its connection to thermodynamics . a quick reference list of core symbols and terminology can be found in label(4.4) in complexity measures the role played by purity is often misunderstood . a measurement of purity provides an upper bound on not a lower bound because the von neumann entropy is always greater than or equal to the seconrder rényi entropy . therefore substituting this relationship into the expression for rcc eq . a purity measurement can only provide an upper bound on complexity . it cannot be used to prove a lower bound on complexity ; its more appropriate role is as a sanity check tool . a correct understanding is that high purity in itself does not guarantee a large rcc lower bound . a meaningful lower bound must originate from the distinguishability of the state relative to the reference state . this distinguishability is quantified by the success rate of hypothesis testing a high occupation probability on a loank projection or a classical entropy that is far from the uniform distribution rather than by purity itself . in contrast the three operational principles proposed in this chapter can all provide rigorous lower bounds . detailed protocols for the three principles mentioned above can be found in appendix and their technical details and boundary subsection(limitations and open questions) label(6.2) the rigor of the rcc framework is built upon several key assumptions which also define its applicability boundaries and the open questions that remain to be explored . it is worth emphasizing that within a fixed subspace all pure states have the same leading term for rcc . as an informatioheoretic lower bound rcc aims to set a baseline for functions based on von neumann entropy . the most central theoretical assumption lies in the strict commutativity of the reference set which makes it naturally suited for systems defined by abelian window)label(sec 63) the core definition of the rcc framework while ensuring structural fairness also introduces a profound paradox from this global perspective all pure states —whether they are simple product states or graph states with highly noocal entanglement—possess the same maximal leading term of complexity . this conclusion of pure state degeneracy severely contradicts both our physical intuition and practical computational experience as it seems to completely erase the vastly different internal correlation structures of different quantum states which are precisely what determine the true computational cost of preparing them . the resolution to this paradox is rooted in a more profound physical principle complexity is not an intrinsic absolute property of a quantum state but rather a relational property that emerges from the interaction between an observer and the system . the structural complexity of a state is latent within its internal global correlations ;to quantify it one must actively reveal it through a physical probe . this physical probe is precisely the observational window introduced for thermodynamic analysis in sec .  this mathematical tool formalizes a physically realistic observer with finite capabilities . such an observer cannot perceive the entire global pure state of the system at once but can only interact with the system through a specific perspective limited by their capabilities e.g. being able to perform only local measurements . the core insight is that when such a constrained observer examines a pure state with a complex internal structure the state will appear as a mixed state within their window due to the inability to resolve its delicate global correlations thus giving rise to an emergent noero entropy . crucially the magnitude of this emergent entropy is a direct fingerprint of how the internal correlation structure of the pure state responds to that specific mode of observation . a window that is highly aligned with the states structure will reveal its latent complexity to the greatest extent ; whereas a simple product state will remain simple under any local window and its emergent entropy will be minimal . therefore by shifting the theoretical framework from the global to the observatioindoependent we not only solve the technical problem of pure state degeneracy but more importantly we elevate rcc into a more complete dynamic theory . this theory acknowledges the central role of observation in defining physical reality and provides a conceptually profound and practically feasible pathway for quantifying the structural complexity of different pure states . to this end we further rigorize the concept of the observational window from hyperrefsec 54(sec . 5.4) defining it as a conditional expectation acting on is a unital completely positive and tracreserving cptp and idempotent quantum channel corresponding to some von neumann subalgebra and satisfying the condition of compatibility with the reference vacuum . this compatibility is an extension of the principle of structural fairness ensuring that the observation process does not distort the zero point of complexity . using the monotonicity of relative entropy and the fact that one can obtain and thus . more importantly this algebraic structure endows complexity with a hierarchical monotonicity if the observational capability is enhanced i.e . then the idempotency of the conditional expectation ensures which in turn implies thereby yielding a welehaved complexity hierarchy . to connect this theoretical framework textit(we provide a rigorous framework in appendix for calculating a controllable conservative lower bound on complexity in the presence of energy or mode cutoffs . ) section(conclusion) label(7) this paper has systematically proposed and constructed the theoretical framework of referencontingent complexity aiming to provide a selonsistent and operational solution for addressing the lontanding structural fairness problem in quantum information science . starting from first principles we formalize the intrinsic structure of a system—whether it originates from symmetries conservation laws or deliberate encoding—as an a priori reference set and using this as a benchmark we define complexity as the information gap of a quantum state relative to this structured background a gap which can be measured by relative entropy . this construction fundamentally ensures that our measure only prices the norivial quantum information that must be generated at the cost of computational resources . the core theoretical contribution of this paper is the proof of a main theorem theorem 3.1 which establishes that is a rigorous theoreevel lower bound on the optimal number of atomic instruction steps for any universal quantum circuit . this theorem is not only mathematically rigorous but its physical meaning also reveals a profound connection between the informatioheoretic properties of a state the information gap and the spectral skew and the computational cost of the dynamical process . to ensure the physical relevance of this theory we have further proposed a set of operational principles based on quantum hypothesis testing projective witnesses and dephasing entropy bounds detailed in chapter demonstrating that the lower bound from can be estimated through experiments and numerical simulations thereby connecting an abstract theoretical concept with concretely measurable physical observables . as a theoretical tool the value of is manifested in its broad application interfaces . we have shown the welehaved mathematical properties it possesses as a proper resource measure such as monotonicity under free operations sec .  we have elucidated how it complements and deepens the theoretical framework for the performance frontier of quantum dynamics elevating a procesependent complexity measure to a state function determined solely by the final state as shown in sec .  furthermore we propose that the structural fairness of makes it a promising candidate to play a key role as a calibration benchmark in the exploration of fundamental physical questions such as the complexiteometry holographic duality sec .  in summary referencontingent complexity provides a foundational and structurally fair theoretical tool for understanding and quantifying the physical costs of quantum computation . it offers a unified meter stick for us to compare and diagnose increasingly complex quantum algorithms and hardware platforms and opens up a solid and operational new path for exploring the deep unification of information dynamics and spacetime geometry . we are well aware that the establishment of any theoretical framework is merely the beginning of an exploration not its end . many theoretical properties of such as the tightness of its lower bound conjecture 6.1 its generalization to systems with nobelian symmetries and its quantitative connection to quantum chaos and thermodynamics remain open questions full of opportunities . we hope that this work will inspire more theoretical and experimental explorations within the field jointly advancing towards a deeper understanding of the fundamental concept of complexity in the quantum world . appendix section(detailed mathematical proof of the main theorem) label(a) this appendix aims to provide a complete and label(c.1) to ensure the rigor of our theoretical derivations in appendix we directly define the optimal circuit complexity as the minimum required number of serial atomic instruction steps . this definition is clear and unambiguous within the framework of algorithmic information theory . here we aim to provide a supplementary explanation from a physics perspective for this formal definition to clarify its connection with the parallel quantum circuit models widely used in physical reality . in concrete hardware implementations quantum circuits are typically executed in a parallel fashion . the computational resources of a parallel circuit are usually characterized by two dimensions the depth of the circuit i.e . the number of parallel time layers and the degree of parallelism of each layer i.e . the number of noonflicting operations that can be performed simultaneously in that layer . the total computational workload or total cost of a circuit is physically proportional to the sum of all atomic operations performed across all parallel layers . our definition of is conceptually a direct quantification of this total physical cost . it is equivalent to the total length of an optimal parallel circuit after it has been flattened into an equivalent serial instruction sequence . this method of definition not only maintains a close connection to physical reality but also maximizes the simplicity and universality of the theoretical derivations . subsection(closeorm solution and usable approximations for the bootstrap inequality) label(c.2) the main theorem eq . leads section(introduction)label(sec 1) consider a quantum circuit consisting of finitely many unitary operations in which all operations are paiise commuting . examples include instantaneous quantum polynomial ; commuting local hamiltonian ; or certain implementations of an oracle function in quantum algorithms ; . such a circuit will be called a commuting circuit hereafter . now suppose a quantum machine given to us can handle more than one commuting operation at the same time if certain conditions imposed by the machine are met . in other words some operations are parallelizable depending on the machine . this concept of parallelizability leads to the notion of emph(depth) of a circuit in implementing a function by the logic circuit multiple choices for the circuit construction are often allowed and thus the most beneficial one is better chosen ; . given that the number of bits is fixed a circuit with a shorter depth is often considered efficient as it means the parallelizability is fully exploited . for this reason among others optimizing the depth of a circuit is an active area of research ; . this work uncovers the relationship between the depth optimization of commuting circuits and the problem in graph theory that is known to be nard . the relation then introduces a circuit optimization strategy in a natural way . the results are summarized as follows begin(itemize) item depth optimization of a commuting circuit is shown to be polynomial time reducible in the number of operations to solving the vertex coloring problem . the opposite direction is also proven to hold meaning that the two problems are equivalent . item the reduction implies emph(any algorithm) for the vertex coloring can be utilized to optimize a commuting circuit . item the strategy is applied to optimize circuits for finite field multiplications and additions by quantum fourier transform qft . the first application exhibits the improvement upon maslov et al.s design ; and the second one gives tradeoff options for drapers quantum addition ; . end(itemize) the paper is organized as follows . preliminaries are given in section;. main idea and proofs are given in section;. applications are examined in section ; and some discussions are noted in section;. section(preliminaries)label(sec preliminary) this section introduces necessary definitions known facts and related works . readers are assumed to be familiar with the basics of quantum information ; . subsection(parallel execution of commuting operations)label(sec motivation) the purpose of this subsection is to bring out the motivation . consider a toffoli gate denoted by where are indices of the control bits and is the index of the target bit . let be an ordered set and consider a quantum circuit implementing gates in . notice that the two gates share the same control bit indexed by 3 and we assume a quantum machine cannot execute these gates simultaneously . therefore in this case we count the depth of as . definition of the depth is given below . now let . the depth of is 3 since and do not share any control or target bit thus the two gates are simultaneously executable by the machine assumed . there is a way to further decrease the depth of the circuit . notice that the gates in are paiise commuting ; any permutation of the four gates leads to the same behavior . if one picks an order and then the depth becomes . subsection(gate ordering problem)label(sec gatrdering) begin(definition)commuting operations 	two unitary operations written by matrices are emph(commuting) if and only if . end(definition) begin(definition)depth of a circuit 	given a hardware system operations are parallelizable if and only if they can be simultaneously executed on the system . a layer is the maximal set of operations such that the operations are parallelizable . depth of a circuit is the number of consecutive layers to run the circuit . end(definition) be reminded that depth is defined in terms of operations not mere elementary gates . for example in a modular exponentiation circuit for modulus that appears in factoring or discrete logarithm algorithms the modular multiplication takes place times thus if we count the multiplicatioepth it would read . however the multiplication can be further decomposed into additions in which each addition takes another elementary operations resulting in depth of elementary gates for the exponentiation . notice in this example that modular multiplications are all paiise commuting whereas not all elementary gates are commuting during the exponentiation . from now on the term emph(gate) will often be used instead of operation . let be a sequence of gates where the gates are paiise commuting . the problem we want to solve is defined as follows begin(definition)gate ordering 	for a given circuit consisting of commuting gates a gate ordering problem is to reorder the gates in such that the depth is minimized . end(definition) here we do not consider cancelling or replacement of a subcircuit ; for example applying the same cnot gate twice in a row is equivalent to doing nothing but such optimization is not a point of interest . subsection(graph coloring)label(sec grapoloring) a graph is an ordered set where is a set of vertices and is a set of edges denoted by connecting two vertices and . only simple and undirected graphs are considered in this work ; . a graph coloring of is a function where is a set of colors . without loss of generality we will use a convention that the colors are drawn incrementally from the natural numbers . begin(definition)proper coloring 	a proper coloring of is a coloring such that for all . 	label(def coloreraph) end(definition) notice that does not mean . begin(definition)vertex coloring problem 	given a graph a vertex coloring problem is to find a colored graph such that is minimized . label(def grapoloring) end(definition) the term graph coloring frequently refers to vertex coloring throughout the paper . chromatic number of a graph is the smallest number that is required to color the graph . subsection(related works) the optimization of a logic circuit has long been studied . the minimum circuit size problem asks if a boolean function is computable by a circuit of limited size and several papers of evidence suggest that the problem might be nard ; . in quantum computing recent works show that optimizing a quantum circuit in some occasions is nard ; and specifically in the paper by wetering and amy ; wide range of optimization targets have been considered including ount epth toffolount toffolepth cnoount and so on proving that the quantum circuit optimization is generally hard . along the line of study one of the conclusions drawn from this work is that the depth optimization of a commuting quantum circuit is nard implying that this small class of quantum circuits is already hard to optimize . there exist works on quantum circuit optimization utilizing coloring in graph theory by looking emph(qubits as vertices). for example edge coloring of a graph has been used to optimize the depth of clifford circuits ; or binary field inversion ; . such an approach is natural in the sense that once wires qubits are viewed as vertices and gates are considered as edges interconnecting the wires the result of edge coloring tells which gates are parallelizable because two edges being connected to the same vertex implies they share the same qubit as the reference . on the other hand to our best knowledge this work is the first attempt to make use of a graph in which emph(quantum gates are vertices). the optimization approach developed in this paper uses an algorithm for graph coloring as the core routine . any graph coloring algorithm can be used for example including ones from previous works ; and it will soon be shown that the output of the graph coloring is directly related with the optimized circuit . section(reduction from gate ordering to graph coloring)label(sec main) the gate ordering problem is reduced to the graph coloring problem in this section . the opposite direction is also given in appendix ; showing that the two problems are equivalent . since the graph coloring problem is in nard it implies optimizing a commuting circuit is also hard . title(clique detection using symmetrestricted quantum circuits ) ieeeauthorrefmark(2) tobias roheieeeauthorrefmark(1) dmytro bondarenkoieeeauthorrefmark(1) linus menzelieeeauthorrefmark(1) and claudia linnhofopienieeeauthorrefmark(1) ieeeauthorblocka(ieeeauthorrefmark(1)institute of informatics lmu munich) ieeeauthorblocka(ieeeauthorrefmark(2) email  email ) begin(abstract) we show the application of permutationvariant quantum circuits to the clique problem . the experiment asks to label a clique through identification of the nodes in a larger subgraph . the permutationvariant quantum circuit outperforms a cyclinvariant alternative as well as a standard quantum machine learning ansatz . we explain the behavior through the intrinsic symmetry of the problem in the sense that the problem is symmetric under permutation of both the feature and the label . end(abstract) begin(ieeekeywords) quantum machine learning symmetry discrete symmetry optimization graph problems clique problem end(ieeekeywords) section(introduction) quantum computing has emerged as a promising computational paradigm attracting considerable attention in recent years . with demonstrated advantages over classical algorithms there is a growing expectation that quantum computing will eventually surpass classical methods . however recent developments have seen a slowdown in new quantum algorithms with research momentum shifting toward the domain of quantum machine learning . in this framework quantum circuits are built using parameterized gates which can be tuned to approximate target functions . unlike classical machine learning quantum machine learning leverages a fundamentally different set of operations for function approximation . at a high level classical models are typically composed of linear transformations interleaved with noinear activation functions structured into layers . in contrast quantum circuits impose different constraints on the learning model . parameters are usually embedded into singlubit gates while entanglement is introduced via noarameterized twubit gates that connect qubits . instead of nested layers quantum circuits follow a multiplicative composition shaped by the mathematical formalism of quantum mechanics . this structural distinction allows for the design of specialized quantum machine learning circuits often referred to as ansatzes tailored to specific tasks . in classical machine learning architectural tuning or incorporation of specific layers can adapt the model to a problem’s structure . for instance convolutional neural networks are explicitly constructed to encode translational invariance . more recent innovations such as attention mechanisms provide models with the capacity to learn relevant symmetries from data . quantum machine learning has not yet reached this level of flexibility and incorporating meaningful symmetries into quantum models remains an open challenge . owing to their unique structure quantum circuits may enable learning paradigms that go beyond classical strategies . classical networks express symmetry primarily through their overall architecture—as seen in convolutional networks graph neural networks and to some extent transformeased models —but typically do not encode specific symmetries of individual problems . quantum circuits on the other hand allow for the exact encoding of problepecific symmetries through their multiplicative structure . if the symmetry underlying a physical system or computational problem is well understood—either from empirical insights or theoretical analysis—it can be directly embedded into the circuit’s design . this approach enables a more precise alignment between the quantum circuit ansatz and the problem’s inherent structure which can in turn enhance model performance . in this work we examine the application of symmetrized quantum circuits to the malique problem from computer science . a clique within the graph is a set of nodes that forms a complete graph each node is connected to each other node in the set we utilize a standard graph embedding and ask the quantum circuit to label all nodes that are part of the subgraph . section(related work) in the area of classical neural networks graph problems are generally solved with graph neural networks which operate on the individual edges of a graph . this has found significant application across graph problems able to approximately solve many hard problems on graphs . there is already a quantum analogue of this classical approach the quantum graph neural network with similar applications to graph problems . both approaches work on the individual edges . in this model an isomorphic graph is a different graph and can give different results . in contrast there exists the approach of integrating the global symmetry of the problem into the system . this is termed grounvariant sometimes -equivariant quantum computation . this leads to interesting mathematics and to its successful application to graph problems . the structural difference here is important graph neural network forego a larger symmetry for solutions on particular graphs while grounvariant approaches incorporate the larger symmetry of isometries . section(quantum circuits) the quantum circuits used in the experiments reflect discrete symmetries between the qubits . discrete symmetries can always be expressed through permutations . we realize the permutations on the quantum circuits through operations between qubits . a quantum circuit can be made invariant under the symmetry in brief the restriction on the symmetry can be transported to the lie algebra the generator space . here generators for quantum circuit elements can be grouped together to fulfill the symmetry requirements . the generators can be transported back to the quantum circuits to create permutationvariant quantum circuits . the quantum circuits are shown in table begin(table) captionquantum end(table) we use different symmetries in our quantum circuits . the strongest symmetry available on a qubit level is the permutation symmetry of all possible permutations . each twubit gate needs to connect from each qubit to any other qubit in this setting . the next weaker regular symmetry is the cyclic symmetry . this symmetry is characterized by cyclically shifting each element to the next one such that and so on . this provides a baseline for the architecture . lastly we compare against one of the standard circuits of quantum machine learning the strongly entangling layer implemented by pennylane . the different layer structures are concatenated until approximately the same number of parameters is reached . the target is 120 parameters meaning 40 repetitions in the case of the permutationvariant quantum circuits 30 in the case of the cyclinvariant quantum circuits and three for the stronglntangling layer in the standard ansatz . section(experiments) we test our quantum circuits on the clique problem . within a graph a clique is a set of nodes that is fully connected meaning that each node within the set is connected to every other node in the same set . the features of the data set are erdőényi random graphs and the labels indicate the clique position . the graphs are sampled with a random edge connectivity and are then separated into the label groups . graphs without a clique of at least the desired size are labeled as a blanket expected measurement on all qubits . for graphs containing larger cliques the contained clique is chosen randomly . this is mapped to the quantum computer with a graph embedding where each node in the graph is identified with a qubit and each edge is represented by a cz gate . the label is a measurement pattern such that a qubit is expected to be if it is part of the clique and if it is not . the experiments are set up to detect a lique in the case of 6 qubits and a lique in the case of 8 qubits . other clique sizes show similar results . the quantum circuit essentially needs to learn to identify the fully connected subcircuit hidden in the entanglement operation of the cz gates and then put out the corresponding amplitudncoded labels for the measurement . with the different quantum circuit symmetries it is possible to figure out whether the desired solution has a given symmetry in which case convergence is possible or whether it is not subject to that symmetry in which case no convergence should be observed . section(results) begin(figure) captionvalidation set performance of quantum machine learning on problems that exhibit a symmetry . the quantum circuit is then matched to the symmetry . this entails a graph problem formulated as a binary decision problem such as asking whether a graph is connected or bipartite . in the present case the problem is prima facie not invariant under a symmetry the labeling of the nodes directly decides where the clique is located . this should lead to worse performance for permutationvariant quantum circuits to the point that they should not converge at all . however this overlooks the fact the presented problem is subject to a permutation symmetry since both the feature the incoming graph as well as the label denoting the clique are permutationvariant . in the case of a binary decision problem on a graph the feature individually is permutationvariant . here the permutation transformation has to apply to both the feature and the label for features labels and permutations . this realization opens the door to a deeper study of the phenomenon and broadens the applicability of permutationvariant quantum circuits to cases where the symmetry is intrinsic rather than extrinsic . section*(acknowledgements) mbm acknowledges funding preprint(aip/12ed) title(heuristic ansatz design for trainable ioative digitanalog quantum circuits) section(label(sec intro)introduction) current day quantum computers are inherently limited by both environmental and systematic noise . in the absence of error correction these devices can only support the execution of short depth quantum circuits which fit within their coherence times . within these restrictions the variational model of quantum computing has been developed to explore the full potential of current hardware . in a variational quantum algorithm vqa a short depth parametrized quantum circuit is iteratively optimized by a classical crocessor in an attempt to minimize a given cost function . this model has been proven to be universal adapted for a wide variety of tasks notably the variational quantum eigensolvers vqes designed to approximate the ground energy of hamiltonians hamiltonian simulations the quantum approximate optimization algorithm qaoa designed to give approximate solutions to combinatorial optimization problems quantum circuit compilers machine learning among others . despite the benefits offered by the variational model inaccurate results arising from gate imperfections and restricted circuit depth remain a prime concern . one pathway towards alleviating these limitations is the use of digitanalog quantum circuits which alternate between quantum gates and entangling natural hamiltonian evolutions reducing the circuit dependence on entangling gates of limited fidelity . a typical example is the use of the lonange ising interaction in trapped ioased quantum computers which has been applied to quantum hamiltonian simulations qaoa compilation and used as an entangling layer in vqe circuits . in the same fashion has proposed to use this interaction as a substitute to the problem hamiltonian exponent to generate a qaoike sequence capable of minimizing general symmetric combinatorial problems . the performance of this approach strongly depends on the choice of ion interactions referred to as ansatz hyperparameters . indeed problem agnostic hyperparameters can lead to trainability limitations induced by a large circuit expressivity or by cost landscapes plagued with local minima . on the other hand as demonstrated in certain problepecific ion native ansatz hyperparameters can significantly improve the algorithmic performance yet a procedure to identify them has been lacking so far . following the framework in we develop an approach for identifying hyperparameters suitable for minimizing specific problem instances . for a qaoike ansatz we propose a heuristic based on optimizing a single layer circuit expectation value alternately over variational and circuit hyperparameters using the block coordinate descent method see e.g the proposed heuristic is benchmarked by performing hamiltonian minimization for the sherringtoirkpatrick sk model from to qubits with the coupling coefficients sampled from the standard normal distribution . this is a widely studied model in condensed matter physics arising as a mean field approach to spin glasses . we demonstrate that the proposed heuristic identifies an ansatz structure which provides a favorable optimization landscape . when compared to standard qaoa and the previous approach proposed in we establish that our heuristic ameliorates the optimization and notably reduces the circuit depth required to solve a problem . the paper is structured as follows . sec . provides an outline of the ion native digitanalog circuit implementation based on the lonange ising interactions . in sec . we introduce a heuristic for searching problepecific hyperparameters of the ion native ansatz that ameliorate the optimization in vqa . sec . shows the numerical results where we benchmark the proposed heuristic on random instances of the sk model and investigate how the choice of hyperparameters affects the ioased qaoa performance . sec . summarizes and discusses the results . vspace(-0.5em) section(label(sec qaoa)ion native quantum ansatz) subsection(global ion interaction) trapped ioased quantum computers are mostly known for their fully connected architecture which allows executing entangling gates between any pair of ions in a trap . the interaction between ions is turned by the excitation of collective ion oscillation modes i.e . phonons at specific frequencies under laser radiation . if however the driving frequency is tuned far from the phonon frequencies dispersive regime the phonons are only virtually excited inducing the evolution under the effective hamiltonian for details see appendix with being pauli operator applied to the -th qubit . the coupling coefficients in eq . are given by here the matrix depends on the spectrum of phonon frequences lamicke parameters which quantify the displacement of the -th ion in the -th phonon mode and laser detuning from the carrier frequency . the matrix thus can be precalculated and kept fixed for details see appendix . a characteristic feature of the interaction is that it can be controlled in the experiment by varying the rabi frequencies induced by a laser field individually for for minimizing the energy we use the block coordinate descent bcd . this method alternately optimizes the cost function with respect to each block of variables and . one of the main advantages of bcd is that it allows to optimize each block of variables by methods which take into account specific properties of the problem see e.g the algorithm starts by sampling a random initial guess for hyperparameters uniformly distributed on . then it proceeds to the main bcd iterations loop where the energy is minimized alternately over and . on each iteration of the bcd loop the current approximation for hyperparameters is fixed and the energy is minimized over a pair of variational parameters for details see appendix . once this step is complete the bcd convergence criteria is checked . here is the optimized energy on the -th iteration . if the criteria is met the algorithm terminates and returns as the optimal ansatz configuration . note that the tolerance in eq . is chosen empirically . for the combinatorial optimization problems considered later encoded into traceless hamiltonians was set to . in these settings the criteria requires a prior knowledge of the ground state energy which is typically not accessible in real experiments . in this case one should either introduce a new empirical convergence criteria or run the algorithm multiple times to choose the best ansatz configuration . begin(algorithm)h caption(heuristic for searching a welrainable hyperparameters configuration of the ion native ansatz for a specific problem hamiltonian.) label(alg plagued by multiple local minima . this is a serious limitation for the trainability of variational quantum algorithms which only worsens upon increase of the circuit depth . in contrast the configuration trained by the proposed heuristic provides a more favorable optimization landscape with a single pronounced global minimum see fig.b which is about 2.7 times deeper as compared to the function value becomes exponentially suppressed as increases . the gorge however can be widened by restricting the range of to the vicinity of the global minimum . if the minimum is located in the region of small this can effectively be realized by rescaling by a factor as as a result the narrow gorge widens as shown at fig.c while the energy starts to behave almost like a convex function . in order to find the optimal scaling factor we construct a cost function that estimates the fraction of the parameter space that corresponds to energy bellow a certain value for details see appendix . this cost function is maximized to find . thus the approach for searching problepecific hyperparameters of the ion native ansatz consists of two stages . first the algorithm alternately minimizes the energy over the variational and hyperparameters to find the configuration that provides a favorable optimization landscape . second the optimal scaling factor for is found to stretch the desired part of the cost landscape . this is achieved by maximizing the fraction of parameter space below a certain energy threshold . as a result the heuristic identifies the configuration that allows to significantly improve the circuit trainability for layers as demonstrated in the next section . note that the proposed method requires evaluating the energy only for a single layer ansatz which is efficient in terms of computational time and is accessible in the experiment . however the bottleneck of this heuristic is the optimization of the cost over on each bcd iteration . the cost function with respect to is -dimensional while the shape of the optimization landscape is unknown . as increases this step of the heuristic can become more challenging for standard optimization techniques . <caption start>fraction of sk instances section(label(sec conclusions)conclusions) digitanalog quantum circuits provide a promising tool for reducing algorithms dependence on limited fidelity entangling gates . a notable example of this approach is the ion based quantum architecture as it naturally supports the long range alll interaction . the latter can be controlled on a real quantum device by varying intensities of the applied laser fields . as evidenced by a recent proposal of the ion native ansatz for combinatorial optimization the algorithmic performance strongly depends on the choice of interaction parameters called ansatz hyperparameters . identifying a suitable configuration of these hyperparameters however can itself be a challenging problem . in this work we addressed the problem of identifying hyperparameters of the ion native ansatz suitable for minimizing specific problem hamiltonians . we proposed a heuristic for searching a welrainable ansatz configuration based on a single layer optimization . the heuristic uses the block coordinate descent method for minimizing the energy alternately over variational and hyperparameters . the obtained hyperparameters are then rescaled by a factor which maximizes the fraction of variational parameters space below a certain energy threshold . this allows to eliminate a potential narrow gorge problem in the optimization landscape . the proposed heuristic has a significant advantage as it requires evaluating the energy only for a single layer which has a low computational cost and is relativelly easy to access in an experiment . we benchmarked the proposed heuristic on random instances of the sherringtoirkpatrick sk model with interaction couplings sampled from the standard normal distribution . we demonstrated that our heuristic obtains ansatz hyperparameters that provide a favorable single layer cost landscape where the energy behaves almost like a convex function with a single global minimum located in a pronounced well . these high trainability properties are extended to deeper circuits ameliorating the optimization . similar results were observed for maut on random and regular graphs . in addition we observed the interplay between the trainability and expressibility of different ion native ansatz configurations . by choosing a problepecific configuration of we restrict the ansatz expressibility tuning it to prepare specific quantum states out of the whole hilbert space . we systematically studied the heuristic performance on random sk instances for system sizes up to 15 qubits . for each the performance was measured as the fraction of 100 sampled sk instances solved in the ioased qaoa with problepecific hyperparameters . we showed that this fraction evaluated at the circuit depth increases after each training cycle . after four of these cycles 88 - 97% of problem instances were solved at layers for from 5 to 10 . moreover we calculated the fraction of solved sk instances as a function of and found that more than 80% of all instances can be solved using no more than layers for the considered system sizes . identical experiments for qubits demonstrated no significant performance degradation . finally the obtained numerical results were compared to the performance of standard qaoa . for a given problem size we found that the ion native qaoa strongly outperforms the standard one in terms of the fraction of solved instances . compared to the standard implementation ion native qaoa enhanced with the proposed heuristic exhibits a much faster performance improvement with circuit depth . moreover the ion native qaoa experiences a lesser performance degradation as the system size increases . the intuition behind the proposed heuristic can be understood as follows . by minimizing the expectation value at depth one it identifies an ansatz capable of boosting the amplitudes of certain low energy states . consequently at larger depths the ansatz can approximate one of those low energy states . as a result the prepared state can be close to the ground state  - allowing us to classify an instance as solved  - or close to one of the low energy excited states which would be considered a suboptimal solution . indeed we observed that training cycles which did not succeed in preparing the true solution were approximating one of the low energy excited states . in this work we focused on the preparation of the ground state yet in the regime of a large scale combinatorial optimization these suboptimal solutions can equally be considered acceptable . thus the heuristic can be expected to be useful for large scale problem instances as well . this also allows us to conjecture that a similar approach can also be implemented for other problems not limited to combinatorial optimization . we believe these results demonstrate the advantages of the ion native ansatz which in addition to being naturally implementable on a trapped ions quantum computer can be tuned to drastically improve the algorithmic performance as well as to reduce the circuit depth required to solve a problem . this is crucial for implementing variational quantum algorithms on neaerm quantum computers . vspace(1em) section*(acknowledgments) we are grateful to evgeny anikin for providing the code for simulating a chain of equal to . the optimization of the qaoa energy was performed by means of a layerwise inspired heuristic . this method iterates over the qaoa circuit depth starting from a single layer that is optimized with respect to two variational parameters . on each iteration a new layer is added and optimized separately over its variational parameters while keeping all other parameters from the previous layers fixed . this step is followed by the simultaneous optimization over all variational parameters for the whole qaoa circuit . for optimization we once again used the fg optimizer . on each step of this layerwise training heuristic we started the optimizer from 25 random initial points sampled uniformly in the parameter space and chose the best result . in order to find a global minimum we performed 10 runs of this layerwise training for each circuit depth in our qaoa simulations choosing the result with the smallest energy . section(label(appendix stateprep)state preparation combinatorial problem one only needs to find the depth of a circuit that can prepare an arbitrary bit string state. for the case of a -symmetric ansatz and problem hamiltonian the latter translates to preparing a ghike states of the form . importantly the ansatz possesses certain symmetries with respect to hyperparameters . specifically given a state prepared using ansatz with hyperparameters one can note begin(eqnarray) label(a flip) x m ket(psibmbetabmgammaa j)ket(psibmbetabmgamma -1^(delta (jm)a j). end(eqnarray) in other words flipping the -th bit in the prepared state is equivalent to flipping the sign of . by extension flipping several qubits is equivalent to changing the signs of the corresponding hyperparameters . as a consequence the same circuit depth is required to prepare any bit string  - or rather its symmetrized version which respects the symmetry of the ansatz . thus the minimization of all diagonal hamiltonians of a given size requires the same circuit depth at least in principle. this argument evidently ignores how easy it is to train such circuits as well as how to properly adjust the ansatz hyperparameters . nevertheless this fact can be used to establish a bound on the required depth to solve specific problems . due to property of the ion native ansatz one can restrict the problem to the preparation of any of these states . therefore here we maximize begin(abstract) layout synthesis is mapping a quantum circuit to a quantum processor . swap gate insertions are needed for scheduling ubit gates only on connected physical qubits . with the evencreasing number of qubits in nisq processors scalable layout synthesis is of utmost importance . with large optimality gaps observed in heuristic approaches scalable exact methods are needed . while recent exact and neaptimal approaches scale to moderate circuits large deep circuits are still out of scope . in this work we propose a sat encoding based on parallel plans that apply 1 swap and a group of cnots at each time step . using domaipecific information we maintain optimality in parallel plans while scaling to large and deep circuits . from our results we show the scalability of our approach which significantly outperforms leading exact and neaptimal approaches up to 100x . for the first time we can optimally map several 8 14 and 16 qubit circuits onto 54 80 and 127 qubit platforms with up to 17 swaps . while adding optimal swaps we also report neaptimal depth in our mapped circuits . end(abstract) section(introduction) label(sec introduction) the quantum layout mapping problem takes as input a quantum circuit logical design and a coupling map connectedness between physical qubits . the result is an equivalent quantum circuit mapped to the physical qubits such that any binary operation only happens on connected qubits . besides an initial mapping of logical qubits to physical qubits this also involves the insertion of swap gates . noise is inherent to qubits in noisy intermediatcale quantum nisq processors . additional swap gates increase both the ubit gate count and the circuit depth . in the current nisq era minimizing error is of utmost importance for any practical quantum computing . the error rate depends on the number of gates the fidelity of gates and the depth of the circuit . the optimal quantum layout synthesis is to synthesize a mapping that optimizes one of the above metrics . optimal layout synthesis has been studied before . a nice overview is provided in . several heuristic approaches exist which optimize various metrics . the classical algorithm for heuristic mapping is sabre in qiskit . use the mqt benchmarks for mapping and swapping using a heuristic search space reduction with an algorithm . other approaches used include a* with cost metrics maxsat temporal planning and constraint programming minimizing circuit depth . while heuristic approaches are fast and scalable their suboptimal mappings may result in high error rates . optimizing fidelity with exact approaches can result in circuits with the lowest error rate . however as shown in optimizing fidelity is extremely hard and does not scale beyond small circuits . circuit depth and ubit gate count optimization are better alternatives for scalability . the olsq toolfootnote(olsq tool url( hrefl  //github.com/tbcdebug/olsq) optimizes circuit depth and is built on . a scalable variant olsq2 based on z3 appeared in . the qmap toolfootnote(munich quantum toolkit qmap url( hrefl  //github.com/cdum/qmap) optimizes the number of swap gates and is based on . the same authors introduced the use of subarchitectures . other ideas to improve quantum layout use quantum teleportation . in measurements are placed early so qubits can be reused . in we proposed a tool ynth v1footnote(ynth v1 tool url( hrefl  //github.com/irfansha/ynth/releases/tag/ynt1.ccad23) for swap gate optimization which outperformed both qmap and olsq tools . ynth v1 reduces optimal quantum layout synthesis to classical planning . for maintaining the optimality of the swap gates added ynth v1 adds exactly 1 cnot or 1 swap gate at each time step . in such an approach the hardness increases with the plan length i.e . the number of cnots + swaps . despite the recent progress in ynth v1 and olsq2 deep circuits that require many swaps are still out of reach . paragraph*(contribution) in this paper we provide a sat encoding based on parallel plans with domaipecific information . in particular at each time step we map one swap gate and a group of cnot gates . this reduces the makpan and using domaipecific information we maintain the optimality . we propose tway constraints for cnot dependencies for better dependency propagation . in addition we also provide variations of our encoding with bridges and relaxed dependencies via commutation . in all variations we only add provably optimal number of bridges+swaps . for experimental evaluation we consider two benchmark sets 1 standard benchmarks from previous papers ; and 2 deep vqe benchmarks . for comparison we consider leading neaptimal tool tlsq2 and heuristic sabre . for mapping we consider 4 nisq processors melbourne 14 qubits sycamore 54 qubits rigetti 80 qubits and eagle 127 qubits . we propose three experiments in the first two experiments we map both benchmark sets to the sycamore rigetti and eagle platforms . in the first experiment we compare the number of swaps added by all three tools . in the second experiment we compare swap additions and circuit depth of the mapped circuits with tlsq2 . in the third experiment we compare the effectiveness of bridges and relaxed dependencies in our tool by mapping onto the melbourne platform . here we report the additional number of optimal swaps+bridges . we demonstrate that our encoding can optimally map deep circuits onto large platforms with up to 127 qubits . our tool outperforms the leading neaptimal tool tlsq2 up to 100x while always adding the optimal number of swaps . we show that while adding optimal swaps we also report neaptimal depth in the mapped circuits . we also confirm that heuristic approaches like sabre add too many swaps . section(preliminaries) label(sec preliminaries) subsection(layout synthesis for quantum circuits) label(subsec layoutsynthesis) a quantum circuit consists of a fixed number of logical qubits and a number of quantum gates operations that are applied to some qubits in a particular order . if the output qubit of gate is used as an input qubit of gate we say depends on . the dependencies form a dag directed acyclic graph between the gates . gates that are transitively independent are called parallel and can be applied in any order . any quantum circuit can be decomposed to an intermediate representation with only singlubit gates and cnot gates . viewed classically the binary cnot gate controlleot also known as cx takes two qubits as input and transforms them into i.e . the control qubit determines whether the data qubit is negated . we will also use the swap gate which transforms a qubit pair into . a swap gate can be expressed as a sequence of 3 cnot gates . the singlubit gates will be treated as blacoxes in this paper ; they are distinguished by their name x z h s t etc . but we dont make assumptions on their semantics except in an extension of our method in section . we refer the interested reader to for a detailed introduction to quantum gates and quantum circuits in general . most physical quantum platforms have limited connectivity in which the cnot operations can only be applied on physical qubits that are neighbors in the salled coupling graph . given such a circuit and a coupling graph layout synthesis consists of two phases initial mapping and qubit routing . in initial mapping the logical qubits of the given circuit are mapped to some physical qubits of the platform bijectively . in qubit routing the following constraints must be satisfied begin(itemize) item every gate must be scheduled in an order that respects all dependencies ; item every gate must be applied to the correct qubits taken the mapping into account ; item the ubit cnot gates can only be mapped on connected physical qubits . end(itemize) additional swap gates may be required to swap the values of connected physical qubits to ensure all cnot gates can be mapped . in this paper we use gate count as an optimization metric . in layout synthesis the number of singlubit gates and cnot gates remain unchanged . optimal layout synthesis is thus minimizing the additional swap gates . <caption start>-qubit or circuit with cnot gates.<caption end> <caption start>oircuit with only cnot gates.<caption end> for example figure shows an oircuit with logical qubits horizontal lines . the circuit has singlubit gates boxes with names and cnot gates the dot indicates the control qubit while the indicates the data qubit . let us suppose we want to map this circuit onto the linear ubit platform as in figure . regardless of physical qubit connections singlubit gates can always be scheduled . only the ubit cnot gates are relevant for our optimal synthesis problem . thus we first remove the singlubit gates and only consider cnot gates for the mapping . after finding the optimal mapping the singlubit gates will be reinserted . figure shows the cnot gates in the oircuit . in any valid mapping the dependencies must be respected for example gates and can only be mapped before and after gate respectively . in this example the dependency graph is a total order but note that with 4 qubits parallel cnot gates are possible which can be scheduled in any order . one can observe that the connections of the cnot gates and form a triangle . since the coupling graph does not have a triangle one cannot map our example circuit to the linear platform . at least two swap gates are needed for any valid mapping . figure shows such a mapped oircuit where are mapped to respectively . intuitively the swap gates slice the circuit such that the suircuits do not have any triangles by cnot connections . <caption start>mapped oircuit with 2 additional swaps optimal.<caption end finally singlubit gates can be inserted back respecting original dag dependencies . figure shows the final mapped circuit with optimal swap gates . note that the number of physical qubits can be more than logical qubits . in such cases one can use salled emph(ancillary) qubits to avoid unnecessary swaps . similar to ynth v1 we allow ancillary swapping i.e . a mapped physical qubit can be swapped with an empty physical qubit . <caption start>final mapped oircuit after inserting back singlubit gates.<caption end> subsection(optimal layout synthesis as planning) label(subsec optlsplanning) in ynth v1 we encoded optimal layout synthesis as a planning problem in the planning domain definition pddl specification . as discussed above the reduced circuit with only cnot gates is mapped using additional swaps . later singlubit gates are inserted back to reconstruct the final mapped circuit . in such a planning problem either exactly one cnot gate or one swap gate is scheduled at each time step . a plan with the optimal number of actions corresponds to the optimal number of swap additions . paragraph*(planning as sat) given a boolean formula a satisfiability sat problem is finding an assignment to the boolean variables that makes it a true formula . a planning problem can be encoded as a bounded reachability problem . sequential encoding is a standard sat encoding where each time step encodes a single action . using a sequential encoding one can obtain optimal plans by incrementing the plan length by 1. for instance one could use ynth v1 with madagascar a saased planner to find an optimal mapping . since the optimal plan length for the example oircuit is 8 6 cnots + 2 swaps the sat instance has a makpan of 8. as shown in sequential encoding scales well for moderate circuits however deep circuits are still out of reach . it is consensus that a long optimal plan length can severely impact the performance of saased planners . paragraph*(parallel plans) in literature alternative parallel plan encodings like -step and -step were proposed for scaling heuristic saased planning . the key idea in a parallel plan is to group two or more actions whose preconditions and effects do not conflict . while encodings like -step scale well the optimality is not guaranteed . for a scalable optimal layout synthesis one needs a way to group cnots while still maintaining the optimality . subsection(parallel plans in optimal layout synthesis) label(subsec olsparallelplans) madagascar implements both -step and -step parallel plans . directly using ynth v1 with parallel plan encodings in madagascar does not preserve optimality . in particular there are three main challenges begin(itemize) item more than one swap gate can be applied at each parallel step ; item planner needs to find a partial order in each parallel step satisfying dependencies ; item relaxing cnot dependencies within a parallel step is not trivial in a pddl specification . end(itemize) in this paper we directly encode layout synthesis as a sat problem to circumvent the encoding challenges in a pddl specification . in our encoding we allow exactly one swap gate at each parallel step . thus the number of parallel steps corresponds to the optimal swap additions . further we use domaipecific information from layout synthesis to relax cnot dependencies within a parallel step . in particular we make two observations begin(itemize) item the qubit mappings do not change between two consecutive swap gates ; item given a set of cnots one can always reconstruct a partial order with dag dependencies . end(itemize) we take advantage of the partial order reconstruction and drop dependency constraints within a parallel step . the sat solver can now choose exactly one swap and a group of cnots in each parallel step . cnot gates in different time steps still need to respect the original dag dependencies . the full sat encoding is later discussed in detail in section . for our example a parallel plan with a makpan of 3 is sufficient see figure instead of 8. at time step 0 along with the initial mapping a group of cnot gates are also mapped . from time step 1 exactly one swap gate and a group of cnot gates are mapped . note that the satisfying assignment returned by a sat solver only specifies that begin(itemize) item logical qubits are mapped to respectively ; item swap gates on and are applied at time steps respectively ; item gates are applied at ; item gates are applied at ; item gate is applied at ; end(itemize) in mapped circuit reconstruction we use the dag dependencies to order the group of cnots in each time step . in the literature an smt based encoding is applied in tlsq2 which also groups cnot gates between consecutive swap gates . they optimize makpan of their defined problem . however longer makpan may result in better swap count and circuit depth . in our experiments we indeed observe suboptimal solutions by tlsq2 in both metrics . subsection(incremental sat solving) label(subsec incrementalsat) conflict driven clause learning cdcl is a key part of stathrt sat solving . when solving similar instances one can reuse the learned clauses . incremental sat solving allows solving a sat instance given an assumption of a partial assignment . essentially by using different assumptions multiple instances can be solved while reusing the learned clauses . in problems like planning one needs to refute up to plan length for optimal plans . by adding assumptions encoding that the goal is reached in the current iteration one can solve a planning instance incrementally . section(tway parallel sat encoding) label(sec twowaysat) in this section we implement the ideas discussed above . we provide an incremental sat encoding that applies the idea of parallel plans in layout synthesis . table describes the main variables used in the encoding . algorithm describes the structure of our encoding . in every time step a group of cnots are applied . from time step 1 each incremental step adds one extra swap . we generate a set of variables for cnot and swap constraints at each not used the semantics of the unary or binary gates except the swap gates . the previous encoding could also be used to map circuits with for instance binary cz gates instead of cnot gates . if we take the semantics of the gates into account there are more opportunities to optimize the circuits . while a complete rynthesis of the circuit is beyond the scope of this paper we want to illustrate some known techniques that can further reduce the number of swap gates . we emphasize that we now change the optimization problem by allowing more solutions and that the extensions are specific for cnot gates . our main purpose is to show that our proposed encoding can be easily extended to incorporate these techniques known as bridges and relaxed dependencies . we also note that the encoding can be easily restricted to disallow the use of ancillary qubits . paragraph*(bridges) <caption start>cnot gates after initial mapping.<caption end> using a bridge one can apply a cnot on disconnected physical qubits . for instance the bridge in fig . together implements a cnot between and which implements after the preceding swap . we limit ourselves to bridges of distance 2 . observe that the bridge introduces 3 extra cnot gates so the cost is the same as a swap gate . however the result is different since a bridge does not swap the qubits . this might be an advantage depending on the rest of the circuit . in it was shown that using bridges can reduce the overall cnot count . we adapted our optimal tway sat encoding by allowing to add either a single bridge or a single swap gate at each time step . if a bridge was added the corresponding cnot gate is regarded as scheduled . so both options cost exactly 3 cnot gates . the sat solver will find a solution with the minimal sum of bridge or swap gates . our experiments will show that we indeed find better solutions with bridges . paragraph*(relaxed dependencies) <caption start>cnot gates after initial mapping.<caption end> the authors of consider gate commutation rules for quantum layout mapping . commutation and cancellation rules on and cnot gates are also used in to reduce the number of ates . for instance two subsequent cnot gates on the same control qubit or on the same data qubit can be commuted without changing the semantics . also single ike gates like the zstand -gates commute with the control bit of a cnot while ike gates like the xand -gates commute with its data bit . this added freedom can be exploited by permuting the cnot gates they can be grouped in a convenient manner so less swap gates are needed . for instance in fig . and can be commuted since they share their control bit . as a result we can now find a solution that requires only 1 swap gate fig . while still respecting the linear coupling graph . the gate commutation rules can be incorporated in our optimal tway sat encoding by computing a relaxed dependency graph . in the example above we consider as a dependency for and but and are considered independent . we stress that the relaxed dependencies must also take the unary gates into account for instance and cannot be commuted since there is a ate in between cf . fig .  in our tool we compute the relaxed dependency graph before removing the unary gates . we then generate the encoding as presented before replacing the dependency graph with the relaxed dependency graph . this guarantees an optimal layout mapping minimal number of swaps given the specified commutation rules . our experiments show that relaxed dependencies can indeed provide better solutions . paragraph*(noncillary mapping) the actual cost of ancillary qubits in practical quantum computing depends on the context . we provide optimal layout synthesis without any ancillary swaps as an option . note that the resulting encoding may require more swap gates than when allowing ancillary qubits . this option can be encoded in our tway sat encoding by simply restricting the swap gates to cases where both the physical qubits are already mapped . subsection(design choices) label(subsec designchoices) paragraph*(redundant cardinality constraints for mapping variables) specifying exactlne constraints eo on logical qubits and aosne constraints ao on physical qubits in the initial time step would be sufficient for correctness . note that once the mapping variables are set in the initial time step the information on bijectivity is propagated to next time steps based on the chosen swap variables . however observe that unrelated to the choice of swap variables some invariants apply to mapping variables in all time steps . essentially the eo and ao constraints are orthogonal to the swap variable assignment . we observed that adding such redundant constraints at each time step significantly improved solving times . apparently this local information can be exploited by the sat solver during clause learning or unit propagation . since we added mostly binary clauses we conjecture that the improved solving time is due to improved unit propagation . paragraph*(tway encoding vs explicit cnot constraints) in this paper we encoded cnot constraints using a tway encoding instead of explicit cnot constraints . we chose tway encoding for two main reasons . first we encode transitive closure for predecessors/successors of cnot gates . explicit constraints for cnot dependencies result in two challenges begin(itemize) item specifying that the predecessors successors of a cnot gate can not be scheduled in later earlier time steps results in a quadratic blop in the cnot gates . item specifying that the predecessors successors of a cnot gate must be scheduled in earlier later time steps results in long clauses . end(itemize) on the other hand the tway encoding expresses this bidirectional propagation implicitly using clauses linear in the number of cnot gates . second in incremental solving in each iteration we need to specify that the goal is reached in the final time step . using the tway encoding we can simply specify that no cnots are delayed in the final step . if we encoded the cnot constraints explicitly we would need to specify that every cnot is scheduled at some time step . to avoid large clauses one would need to use auxiliary variables similar to advanced/delayed variables to keep track of the scheduled cnots across time steps . in our tool we provide the encoding with explicit cnot constraints as an option . section(experimental evaluation) label(sec experimentalevaluation) subsection(experiment design) label(subsec design) we have paragraph*(comparison to olsq olsq2 and tlsq2) in authors showed that tlsq2 significantly outperforms both olsq and olsq2. because of the lack of grouping in olsq and olsq2 the makpan of smt instances generated is very large. since our tool outperforms tlsq2 we do not report results from the other two directly . tlsq2 optimization routines can also be used in our tool to avoid hard unsatisfiable instances when optimality is not needed. paragraph*(comparison to ynth v1 with classical planning) in we showed that ynth v1 based on classical planning outperformed both olsq and qmap . while the approach scales well for mapping circuits up to 9 qubits onto 14 qubits platforms larger circuits are out of reach . for instance ynth v1 timed out on rcadder6 table with 3 hours . ynth2 maps the same instance optimally within 5 minutes onto the 1ubit melbourne platform . ynth v1 does not scale well to the other larger quantum platforms . mapping individual cnots in ynth v1 results in long plan length . as discussed in the same paper long plan lengths increase the difficulty of planning . paragraph*(comparison to qmap and satmap) qmap employs an smt encoding that grows exponentially with the number of physical qubits . even using subarchitectures qmap is unable to map circuits greater than 7 qubits . satmap on the other hand encodes the layout synthesis as a maxsat problem to minimize the number of swaps . it allows the addition of one swap before every cnot and uses maxsat solvers to minimize the number of swaps . as shown in it produces suboptimal solutions and runs out of time even for moderate circuits . paragraph*(comparison with dynamic programming approach) in the authors provided an exact and a heuristic approach for adding swaps and bridge gates . with commutation rules they showed that using bridges can further reduce the optimal cnot additions . our experiments are consistent with the authors observations . their exact approach already takes 12 minutes to map a ubit circuit to ubit platforms and grows exponentially with the number of qubits . paragraph*(comparison to sabre) as observed in experiment 1 it is clear that heuristic approaches such as sabre add too many swaps . adding many swaps not only increases the ubit gate count but also increases circuit depth . however heuristic approaches have their place in the quantum compilation pipeline. as the number of qubits on quantum processors increases it is necessary to employ a hybrid strategy with heuristic and exact approaches . for instance one could use sabre to quickly find a reasonable initial mapping . given such a mapping one can synthesize a swaptimal mapped circuit using ynth2. as in tlsq2 we could use heuristic approaches to get quick upper bounds for neaptimal solving . section(conclusion) in this paper we showed that parallel plans can be adapted to preserve swap optimality in layout synthesis . we have encoded the parallel planning problem directly in sat . we propose a tway encoding in which information is propagated both forward and backward for efficiency . we also demonstrated that our tway sat encoding is compatible with other techniques like bridges and gate commutation rules . the technique is implemented in the opeource tool ynth2 for scalable and optimal layout synthesis of deep circuits. we can optimally map ubit circuits that require up to fact that clifford gates map pauli strings to other pauli strings thereby allowing for a structured simulation process using classical computations . in this work we break down the stetep procedure of the gottesman - knill theorem in a beginneriendly manner leveraging concepts such as matrix products tensor products commutation antommutation eigenvalues and eigenvectors of quantum mechanical operators . through detailed examples illustrating superposition and entanglement phenomena we aim to provide a clear understanding of the classical simulation of clifford gatased quantum circuits .
