highlighted in red.) label(tabsurvey) end(table*) subsection(heuristic) subsubsection(circuit depth) fagan and duncan introduced the first zased quantum circuit optimization algorithm . their optimization strategy moves pauli gadgets towards the inputs and group cnot and tonc gates cnot gates with switched control and target qubits that act on the same qubits . they demonstrate a significant reduction of the cnot gate count by and circuit depth up to for pure clifford circuits . paragraph(architecturware) staudacher et al . add an additional step to the circuit extraction algorithm of backens et al . between the cnot and singlubit gate extraction to target neutratom architectures . instead of using the clifford + t gate set this work targets a gate set that consists of z gates multontrolled phase gates and global single qubit rotations in the xlane . phase gadgets are the native representation of multontrolled phase gates . for identified frontier phase gadgets the fusion rule and reverse gadget fusion rules are applied . potentially missing phase gadgets are added to extract a full multontrolled phase gate . neutratom quantum computers can natively execute multontrolled phase gates and are limited by execution time and the total gate count . especially the global singlubit rotation is an order of magnitude slower than the multontrolled phase gate and the z phase gates . the circuits execution time is computed along the circuit as the sum of individual gates execution time which is assumed to increase with the rotation angle . their approach outperforms the execution time of qiskit compiled circuits from up to primarily due to the reduction in the number of global phase gates . subsubsection(ate count) paragraph(architecturndependent) kissinger and van de wetering use the theoretical framework of duncan et al . to allow semantic preserving optimization of circuits composed of the entire clifford + ate set . their procedure aims to minimize the ate count . their simplification strategies apply local complementation and pivoting to remove pauli spiders spiders with a phase that is a multiple of at the expense of adding phase gadgets . applying the identitemoval and gadget fusion rules efficiently remove the phase gadgets . by rerunning the previous algorithm symbolically it is possible to identify nonlocal phase recombinations that further reduce the ate count . this step is known as phase teleportation . the resulting optimization algorithm is implemented as the standard simplification routine in the pyzx library under the name full reduce . it is found in many optimization pipelines as a preor posrocessing step for ate minimization . the evaluation of a benchmark set that consists of 36 structured standard quantum circuits shows that full reduce improves the stathrt ount on 17% and matches on 72% of the instances . further improvements were achieved when full reduce is paired with the dedicated ate optimizer todd . combining both methods improve the ount in 56 % of the benchmark circuits . the following approaches develop spider nest identities for -parithase operations to eliminate ates from quantum circuits . a spider nest is a zx diagram that consists only of phase gadgets . instead of rules that modify a single or few generators spider nest identities take the full nest into account . munson et al . independently derived the same spider nest identities and generalized them by connecting zalculus and logical and gates . beaudrap et al . introduce the phase gadget elimination phage strategy a systematic method that takes advantage of spider nest identities to reduce the ate count in ziagrams . the core idea of phage is to decompose larger and more complex phase gadgets into simpler and smaller ones . this decomposition allows for the effective application of spider nest identities to eliminate ates . the evaluation of phage on a benchmark set of 35 parameterized circuits reveals that the stathrt ate counts are improved for 21 instances under runtime constraints . paragraph(architecturware) zilk et al . use the phase teleportation algorithm of kissinger and van de wetering to reduce the ate count and the clifford elimination algorithm of fagan et al . to target photonic quantum computers . the first step in their procedure is to express a quantum circuit only as a sequence of hadamard cz and arbitrary hase gates . the resulting circuit is converted to a measurement graph that corresponds to a grapikedefinition ziagram . this ziagram is optimized with the phase teleportation and clifford elimination algorithms . measuremenraphs can be directly converted into hardware instructions . the limiting factor of photonic architectures is the number of available photons and optical instruments . compared to the standard photonic compiler perceval the zased approach successfully compiles all benchmarked circuits and mostly outperforms with respect to the photon count and optical instrument count . subsubsection(qubit count) vandaele et al . introduced an approach to minimize the logical qubit count in ziagrams by systematically reordering and unbending spiders . the core idea is to use the rewrite rules to change the structure of the ziagram such that it is possible to find a vertical cut that reduces the maximum number of wires hence minimizing the logical qubit count . the nard problem of minimizing the number of wires through vertical cuts is formally known as the fixendbags pathwidth problem . consequently finding an optimal solution is computationally expensive for large diagrams . subsubsection(twubit gate count) paragraph(architecturndependent) staudacher et al . demonstrate that an average reduction of the edge count by 23% translates to a twubit gate reduction of 16% by applying a set of gfloreserving rewrite rules identity removal spider fusion local complementation and pivoting . they introduce a new heuristic based on the expected change of the hadamard wire count by the local complementation and pivoting rules . a reduction of the hadamard wire count correlates with the expected reduction of twubit gates . slightly worsening of the cost function was allowed to permit further improvements later on . stochastic and greedy algorithms are used to select the rewriting rules . further integration with the nam framework allowed for greater edge count reductions of 29% that translated into twubit gate reductions of approximately 21%. in a related work holker extends these ideas by focusing on diagrams that preserve the stricter causal flow cflow property . if cflow is preserved the effect of a rewriting rule on the twubit gate count can be exactly quantified from change in the wire count completely bypassing circuit extraction for all intermediate optimization steps . by maintaining cflow holker achieves an average twubit gate count reduction of 20%. ziagrams with cflow have a circuiike structure that allows for a straightforward and efficient extraction . moreover verifying cflow is computationally less expensive than verifying gflow . however it is important to note that only a limited set of rewriting rules namely identity removal and spider fusion are known to preserve cflow . this limitation severely restricts the possible diagram transformations but offers a tradff between the solution quality and verification complexity . the following two optimization strategies use the tket compiler . cowtan et al . demonstrated that the efficient pairwise synthesis of pauli gadgets using tket decreased the average cnot gate count by and improved the twubit depth by . in a subsequent work cowtan et el . showed that a three step optimization routine improves the cnot gate count and depth of the unitary coupled cluster ucc ansatz a subroutine of variational quantum eigensolvers by and i the partition of the ziagram of the ucc ansatz into commuting sets is treated as a graph coloring problem ii the resulting pauli gadgets are converted to phase gadgets and iii the phase gadgets are efficiently synthesized using matroid partitioning . another promising approach to quantum circuit optimization is the aggregation of multiple subcircuits that can be reordered and replaced by optimized template circuits . template circuits are prptimized subcircuits that implement the same program flow as the subcircuit they are meant to substitute . liu et al . introduce a strinased intermediate representation of subcircuits and a template matching algorithm that improves the cnot gate count . although not explicitly relying on rewriting rules for optimization liu et al . employ zalculus to verify the correctness of the intermediate representation and their associated templates . paragraph(architecturware) kissinger et al . introduce the first architecturware optimization algorithm and outperform the existing compiler frameworks quilc and tket . during circuit extraction they restrict the gaussian elimination of the parity map to only include neareseighbor rows using the steineauss algorithm . consequently cnot gates can only act between neighboring qubits . villoria et al . modified the circuit extraction algorithm of backens et al . to target traon computers that are highly dependent on global gates . instead of gaussian elimination the frontier is extracted solving a linear program that ensures only vertices are extracted which can be included in the same global gate . afterwards peephole optimization merges the extracted twubit gates into global gms gates . this algorithm outperforms the qiskit implementation on most quantum circuits . van de griend and duncan develop a two step recursive optimization strategy that considers qubit connectivity restrictions of the underlying quantum architecture thus circumventing the need for an additional routing step by using the notion of phase polynomials . the algorithm introduces a biadjacency matrix between the phase gadgets legs and the attached qubits . for the base recursion step the phase gadget with with the lowest connectivity that is not needed to synthesize other phase gadgets is removed . the selected phase gadget must be a non cutting vertex meaning the column in with the most or entries . afterwards the phase gadgets are synthesized by decomposition into a cnot ladder as shown in figure . the second recursion step removes rows from the remaining phasadget biadjacency matrix by row addition . every row operation adds cnot gates to the ladder . to eliminate excess cnot gates the steineauss algorithm is run on the resulting parity map . winderl et al . adapt the architecturware approach of gorgioso and yeung by replacing simulated annealing with a heuristic search in combination with a dividnonquer strategy . the first step in their strategy is the simplification of the zx polynomial by removing merging and moving phase gadgets . afterwards the ziagram is split into a left parity a right parity and a zx polynomial region . a gaussian elimination optimization algorithm minimizes the cnot count based on the combined cost of the region . the cost of removing a phase gadgets legs is computed by the minimal spanning tree of the architecturaependent connectivity . their novel heuristic based on the shortest path between the control and target qubit of cnot gates is used in conjunction with the steineauss algorithm to synthesize the phase gadgets in both parity regions . the remaining zx polynomial is regrouped from a leased score and following a dividnonquer strategy split into subregions again . these steps are recursively repeated until no zx polynomial remains . both methods are outperformed by other stathrt algorithms such as tket for structured circuits . however the heuristic approach of winderl et al . exhibits better scaling in the qubit count and cnot tree depth compared to the stochastic approach by gogoiso and yeung . huang et al . develop a novel approach for architecturware synthesis of trotter operators . trotterized time evolution operators can be expressed in terms of pauli gadgets . pauli gadgets can be described by exponentiation of pauli strings . each letter of the pauli string corresponds to a pauli gate . the core idea of their approach is to lexicographically reorder the pauli strings that compose the pauli gadgets of the trotter operator . as a result phase gadget legs with the same letter are grouped on the same qubit . reordering of noommuting pauli gadgets is possible because the introduced error trotter error is outweighed by the error that originates from noisy gates . their algorithm iteratively diagonalizes and disconnects qubits . the highest entangled qubit is chosen for the current iteration . the diagonalization step places single qubit clifford gates on the selected qubit until the gadget has either no leg or a z leg. based on the pauli gadget leg the disconnection step introduces two cnot gates and up to two singlubit clifford gates . this disconnection step reduces the entanglement of the selected qubit . the selection of the qubit is determined by an entanglement heuristic . qubit entanglement is calculated from the occurrences of the ate in the pauli string and the length difference between the largest and smallest substrings that exclude the ate . this approach outperforms the stathrt cnot count for random circuits and larger couplluster unitaries . subsection(metaheuristic) subsubsection(twubit gate count) paragraph(architecturndependent) chen et al . improve the twubit gate count by compared to the heuristic approach of staudacher et al . using simulated annealing to partition a quantum circuit into subcircuits that are optimized . in a first step the quantum circuit is divided into sequential layers of gates . per layer one singlubit gate one target and control qubit of multubit gates can act at most on each qubit . subcircuits are groups of sequential layers . starting from a random configuration of subcircuits each circuit is converted into a ziagram optimized and extracted . the resulting circuits are iteratively merged . following a delayed gate approach known gate commutation and substitution rules are used to further improve the circuit depth and gate count . the delayed gate approach is implemented in pyzx under the name basic optimization . for each iteration of the simulated annealing algorithm the starting configuration of the subcircuits is changed . paragraph(architecturware) gogioso and yeung reduce the cnot count for mixed phase gadgets ziagrams by on a grihaped topology . their technique is grounded in the decomposition of phase gadgets and is paired with simulated annealing and cnot conjugation rules . the ziagram is split up into three layers i a left neareseighbor cnot layer ii a right neareseighbor cnot layer and iii a mixed phase gadget ziagram . the cost of implementing a phase gadget is computed from the distance between distinct legs that are mapped onto the topology . this corresponds to the neareseighbor cnot count . the total cost of a circuit is the sum of all its cnot gates . simulated annealing is used to explore different phase gadget mappings . to exploit symmetries the phase gadgets are converted to cnot ladders figure so that gate conjugation rules can be applied . ewen et al . introduce a genetic programming approach for synthesizing shallow quantum circuits with fewer twubit gates from ziagrams . the original quantum circuit is converted into a ziagram that will be evolved via a set of mutation operations . in their work they implement two different categories of mutations . semanticreserving mutations are formed by the rewriting rules of zalculus . semanticreaking mutations such as edge flipping and edge addition introduce new connectivity patterns in the ziagram . although these semanticreaking mutations violate the correctness of the circuit they permit the exploration of a larger statpace at the cost of circuit fidelity . experimental results demonstrate that zased genetic programming can produce welalanced circuit solutions achieving results close to the stathrt for circuit depth circuit fidelity and twubit gate count . subsection(reinforcement learning) subsubsection(metric agnostic) nägele and marquardt implement a scalable and general reinforcement learning framework for the optimization of ziagrams that can be adapted for different metrics . actions are grouped by node and edge impact irrespective of the preservation of gflow or cflow . as a consequence quantum circuit metrics are not considered because of the lack of circuit extraction . in contrast to the rpproaches of riu et al . and mattick et al . the reversibility of rewriting rules is considered beyond spider un/fusion by including the bialgebra rule . furthermore the agent can mask actions to improve the efficiency of training. subsubsection(twubit gate count) riu et al . introduce a rased approach that uses graph neural networks to minimize the twubit gate count . they restrict the set of rewriting rules to gfloreserving transformations . circuit extraction is treated as a blacox simplifying the optimization pipeline . the rl agent is trained to either select and apply a rewriting rule or to terminate the optimization process . the agent can apply multiple rules until it decides to terminate . a reward function guides the decision based on metrics such as the twubit gate count . moreover the rl framework is highly flexible and can incorporate other reward functions such as ate count or circuit depth . a key advantage of this rased strategy is the scalability for larger ziagrams . although the initial training phase can be computationally demanding the resulting agent can generalize its learned strategies to new diagrams independent of their size . among the approaches surveyed the combination of this rased optimization approach with holker’s cfloreserving framework represents one of the most effective strategies to reduce the twubit gate counts in zalculuased circuit optimization . subsection(tree search) subsubsection(metric agnostic) fischbach et al . propose an exhaustive search strategy combined with pruning conditions to optimize zx diagrams . the objective of the search is to find a sequence of rewriting rules that optimizes a given metric . their method explores the statpace using deptirst search dfs and iterative deepening deptirst search iddfs by applying all possible rule combinations . pruning conditions terminate branches of the search tree e.g. if circuit extraction is impossible . despite being a complete search for a rewriting rule sequence that minimizes a given metric the main drawback of their approach is the computational cost . a comparison of their iddfased approach and the ate count obtained by the full reduce algorithm of duncan et al . was performed . the analysis demonstrated equivalent results in 89% of the circuits within a benchmark set of 100 structured circuits . nevertheless one strength of their approach is the metrignosticism ; it is not tied to the optimization of a single metric such as the ate count . they demonstrated its flexibility by targeting the edge count a proxy for twubit gates with the same strategy . while the exhaustive nature of the search makes the approach computationally inefficient for larger circuits it allows for optimal solutions for small sized circuits . mattick et al . propose a hybrid approach that combines rl with a tree search algorithm that uses the full set of standard zalculus rules . their method slightly outperforms the stochastic and gflow preserving techniques of staudacher et al . for random circuits . in this framework the graph neural network replaces the heuristics by learning which and where a rewriting rule should be applied or if the agent needs to stop . the tree search allows to backtrack if not beneficial transformations are encountered . similarly to riu et al . the agent learns where to apply which rule in the ziagram based on a reward function that represents a metric . however at each node of the tree the agent is allowed to perform only one diagram transformation . the use of the complete set of zalculus rewrite rules permits the exploration of a larger statpace at the cost of posrocessing to ensure circuit extraction . the key advantage of this approach is its generality . the framework aims to learn optimal rewrite sequences for any chosen metric and is not limited to minimizing twubit gate counts . section(framework) quantomatic is the first implementation of zalculus for quantum circuit optimization and has been quickly superseeded by pyzx . pyzx is a python library that implements a twtep graph rewriting system to modify a ziagram . each rule consists of a matching and a rewriting function . the matching function returns all occurrences of spiders where it is possible to apply the specified rule . the rewriting function transforms the ziagram based on the rule and provided matches . moreover it offers an implementation of the ate optimization algorithm with the name full reduce . other notable features of pyzx include circuit verification extraction and tight integration into other quantum computing frameworks such as qiskit . quizx is a faster rust implementation of some core features of pyzx by the same project . it offers python bindings and an api similar to pyzx . the munich quantum toolkit provides another implementation of zx calculus written in c++ including support for circuit optimization and verification . section(challenges) label(sec challenges) paragraph(scalability) a major challenge in the optimization of ziagrams lies in the scalability of rulased rewriting approaches especially as small reaorld quantum circuits result in large ziagrams . with an increase in size of ziagrams the computational complexity grows rapidly limiting the practical application of existing techniques to smalcale quantum circuits . current heuristiased optimization strategies typically target a single metric such as reducing the number of nolifford spiders e.g. duncan et al . kissinger et al . and beaudrap et al . or minimizing the number of twubit gates e.g. staudacher et al . holker et al . and fagan and duncan . however while heuristics improve computational performance focusing on a single objective fails to capture the complex features of quantum circuits and how to balance them . we identify the clear need for improved heuristics that can balance multiple metrics to improve the computational performance of existing strategies . recent works have explored rl approaches for diagram rewriting nägele et al . riu et al . mattick et al . demonstrating promising results on smalcale ziagrams . although rl is still computationally expensive the training stage can be seen as an upfront cost as the learned strategies appear to be at least partially generalizable . further enhancement of rased methods on small zx diagrams could allow better optimization results for largcale circuits . moreover the lack of interpretability and the theoretical background as to why some rewriting sequences are more beneficial than others poses additional challenges . incorporating explainable rl could form the basis for new and computationally efficient heuristics that are applicable for largcale ziagrams . another promising research direction is the introduction of intermediate representations that can aggregate subdiagrams and enable more efficient statpace exploration similar to that of liu et al the use of an intermediate representation allows template matching of prptimized subcircuits . chen et al . dynamically group layers into subcircuits . future work should focus on the efficient partition and resynthesis of quantum circuits for several reasons . dividing larger quantum circuits into smaller subcircuits is beneficial because the resulting subdiagrams are smaller and can be optimized efficiently . as the different subdiagrams are independent of each other each instance can be solved in parallel . this flexibility could lead the way for dynamic selection of the optimization algorithm based on the characteristics of each subdiagram . furthermore a subdiagram only needs to be optimized once and can be substituted for further instances . another possible research direction is to allow for the twimensional partition of quantum circuits for improved optimization results using the intermediate representation of liu et al replacing the sa approach that changes the subcircuit partition of chen et al . with an exhaustive search could further improve the results . paragraph(architecturwareness) quantum computing architectures fundamentally differ from each other and offer different advantages and limitations that quantum circuit optimization needs to take into account . there are four dominant quantum architectures currently considered by zased quantum circuit optimization i superconducting ii trappeon iii neutratom and iv photonic quantum architectures . to create executable quantum circuits for superconducting quantum computers spatial information topology qubit connectivity noise and error correction . some work focuses on architecturware synthesis of phase gadgets and polynomials e.g. van de griend and duncan gogioso and yeung and winderl et al . that takes an architectures topology into account others aim to restrict qubit connectivity . however there is no unified framework that combines the different methods . transpilation would be more efficient if ziagram optimization could target a specific architecture without the need for additional optimization steps to consider decoherence gate error routing and error correction . phase gadgets are the native representation of multubit gates in zalculus therefore improving the architecture and topology aware synthesis is a promising field for future research . zalculus is a natural candidate for photonic quantum computing because the architectures measurement graph corresponds to a grapikedefinition ziagram . this equivalence permits the modification of the measurement graph using rewriting rules . as the measurement graph can be directly converted into hardware instructions additional optimization steps are not required . the initial work of zilke et al . demonstrates the effectiveness of zalculus to target photonic quantum computers . upcoming work could extend the approach of zilke et al . to use different optimization algorithms for ate and clifford gate elimination . especially the rpproach of mattick et al . seems to be a promising candidate for photonic architectures as it balances the quality and exploration of the solution . as photonic architectures do not require circuit extraction the quality of the solution is not impacted by posrocessing and circuit extraction . furthermore future work should address photonic architectures with different graph states that compose the measurement graph . the initial work by staudacher et al . proof the feasibility of zalculus when targeting neutratom architectures . in their work they adapt the circuit extraction algorithm of backens et al . to efficiently synthesize the architectures native multubit gates . forthcoming endeavors should include ziagram optimization methods that take the reduction of global phase gates and the preference of multubit gates before circuit extraction into account . the standout features of trappeon quantum computers are the alll qubit connectivity and the use of global gates . villoria et al . modify the circuit extraction algorithm of backens et al . to only extract vertices that take part in the same global gate . phase gadgets are the zalculus equivalent of multubit gates . in the future work could use the notion of phase gadgets during circuit extraction to improve global gate count and grouping. furthermore there is no dedicated zased optimization strategy that targets traon architectures outside of circuit extraction . paragraph(circuit extraction) a significant limitation of zx diagraased quantum circuit optimization is the computational cost of circuit extraction . in the general case circuit extraction is a #ard combinatorial problem . although polynomiaime algorithms exist for ziagrams that preserve the grapheoretic conditions of gflow and cflow only a small subset of rules have been proven to preserve these flow properties . in addition verifying the presence of a flow is computationally expensive with cflow being less demanding than gflow . in the absence of general or causal flow circuit extraction becomes intractable . especially noteworthy are the extraction algorithms of duncan et al . and its extension by backens et al . that form the basis for various architecturware synthesis algorithms e.g. kissinger et al . villoria et al . and staudacher et al we established that many approaches disregard intermediate zx diagrams without the presence of general or causal flow effectively ignoring large parts of the statpace that might contain the optimal solution . future research should focus on methods that explore intermediate zx diagrams without preserving flow properties while keeping the overhead introduced by circuit extraction at a minimum . this can be achieved by improving or avoiding circuit extraction as much as possible . based on quanz et al . subsequent work should aim to improve parallel circuit extraction to speed up other statpace exploration algorithms . a promising research direction is to replace the gaussian elimination of the biadjacency matrix during circuit extraction by a lp . similarly to villoria et al . future lp formulation could include architectural constraints . circuit extraction is an iterative process and the biadjacency matrix only captures the connectivity of the current frontier . therefore the lp only encodes current information and it is not guaranteed that the optimal solution of the current lp results in the best global solution . upcoming work should combine lased circuit extraction with a backtracking algorithm that allows to prune lp solutions that result in unfavorable quantum circuits . another way of providing context for lased circuit extraction is to provide information of the closest already extracted frontier gates for each qubit . it is important to recognize that the circuit properties strongly depend on the circuit extraction algorithm itself . current circuit extraction algorithms replicate spider connectivity by twubit gates potentially increasing the circuit depth and twubit gate count . improvements of circuit extraction algorithms both in computational efficiency and in circuit quality should allow for better optimization results . in particular only the work of villoria et al . treats circuit extraction as a combinatorial problem . consequently efficient formulations beyond lp constraints and solvers for the circuit extraction problem provide a vast field for future endeavors . many nooc approaches require regular circuit extraction e.g. fischbach et al . ewen et al . and riu et al a critical challenge to avoid circuit extraction is that many characteristics of quantum circuits such as the twubit gate count or circuit depth are not native concepts of ziagrams . investigating other approximations of quantum circuit metrics at the ziagram level such as hadamard wires serving as a proxy for twubit gates might reduce the amount of circuit extraction required . a promising first step could be the construction of a surrogate model for circuit extraction that can be quickly evaluated by different approaches . paragraph(multbjective optimization) the approaches presented in this survey are designed to primarily target one metric . nevertheless it does not suffice to optimize one metric alone to capture the complexity of current quantum computing architectures . some works follow a lexicographic approach in which one metric after another is improved . a typical example is to first run the elimination of the ate by and then optimize the twubit gate count on the resulting ziagram e.g the work of ewen et al . suggests that the best ziagram results in a circuit close to its best known quantum circuit counter part for circuit depth and twubit gate count . however on the noarget metrics the best circuits perform worse than their zased counterparts . so far there exist no deliberate multbjective optimization approaches applied to zased quantum circuit optimization that aim to find a tradff between fundamentally different metrics . multbjective optimization seems to be a promising candidate for architecturware optimization where a tradeoff between independent metrics and different architectural specifications such as qubit connectivity and spatial dimensions is required . bridging the gap towards multbjective optimization would greatly simplify the transpilation pipeline resulting into an integrated and potentially less computationally demanding framework . paragraph(ziagram feature encoding) despite many advances in ziagram optimization and circuit extraction techniques a fundamental question remains what features of a ziagram actually predict or determine the quality of the resulting quantum circuit ? while some connections between the ziagram and the quantum circuit are trivial e.g. the number of -phase spiders directly translates to the number of ates other features are only an approximation or not translated at all . the example we saw before was that the number of hadamard edges and the overall spider connectivity serve as a proxy to estimate the twubit gate count . further research on the mapping between ziagram characteristics and quantum circuit properties could enable the development of better optimization methods that explicitly account for architectural constraints . especially the inclusion cumulative gate error rates qubit connectivity limitations and coherence time would alleviate the need of a full transpilation pipeline . such mappings could serve as a surrogate model that allows quicker heuristic or learninased optimization without repeatedly requiring circuit extraction and transpilation to assess the quality of the solution . furthermore we propose the systematic addition of characteristics that form a composite metric that aggregates information from features derived from the ziagram properties of the logical quantum circuit and characteristics of the final transpiled and executable circuit . investigating such composite metrics allows to dynamically evaluate characteristics based on the current solution quality and computational cost . such approaches would allow to identify the relative importance of individual features in determining overall circuit quality . for example it is unnecessary to take into account accumulated gate error and routing if the initial features already indicate an unfeasible solution . this adaptive composite metric would allow to exclude or adjust certain optimization steps based on the balance between the expected quality of the solution and the computational cost of fully evaluating that metric . by quantifying this tradff the composite metric could be added to many methods that require a cost function while also championing a full compilation workflow without being explicitly designed for it . section(conclusion) this survey provides an overview of quantum circuit optimization using zalculus with an emphasis on optimization techniques and target metrics . the surveyed works demonstrate that zx calculus offers a powerful compact and universal framework that enables optimizations beyond traditional circuievel techniques . this survey identified that the adoption of zased methods is impeeded by scalability issues a reliance on singlbjective heuristics and the computational cost of circuit extraction . several promising research directions emerge future work must expand beyond singletric optimization and adopt multbjective optimization that jointly consider architecturndependent and architecturware metrics . additionally there is a clear need to link ziagram and quantum circuit characteristics potentially through surrogate models or composite metrics that alleviate the computational cost of circuit extraction . furthermore circuit extraction could be improved by leveraging combinatorial optimization with the potential inclusion of architectural constraints . finally more approaches should take into account the underlying quantum computing architecture . especially trappeon neutratom and photonic devices are underrepresented . overall zalculus is positioned as an intermediate representation for circuit optimization that is capable of bridging diagrammatic reasoning with architectural constraints of current and future quantum hardware . improvements of heuristics scalability and explainable learninased methods are necessary to design algorithms that handle efficiently the noerminating nature of zalculus . in summary zalculus is a candidate for an integrated framework that allows architecturndependent and architecturware quantum circuit optimization for current and future quantum computing hardware . between and -qubit circuits and the inherent structural shift that arises as problem size increases . subsection(interpretation of components) the first contribution to performance loss captures the discrepancy between the empirical reward observed during training and the true expected reward on the -city task . it reflects the classical generalization behavior of learning systems the effective capacity of -equivariant qnns scales as implying that the sample complexity grows polynomially with the problem size . as the number of training episodes increases decays as showing that sufficiently extensive training can make this term negligible . importantly this component establishes a floor on achievable transfer performance weak learning on the source task inevitably propagates to the target . the second contribution is the novel element of our analysis and isolates the cost of transferring parameters across problem sizes . the first term in quantifies the generator mismatch because the equivariant circuit generators scale as for the source and for the target reusing induces a systematic discrepancy . this penalty grows linearly with and scales with both the norm of the parameters and their maximal magnitude reflecting the degree to which the learned circuit is tuned to the -qubit dynamics . the second term captures the structural shift between the two tasks . by appealing to euclidean tsp regularity assumptiona6 we bound the difference in optimal performance as which grows smoothly with the problem size gap . together these terms guarantee that transfer degradation is gradual rather than catastrophic in sharp contrast with noquivariant circuits where symmetry breaking can cause performance collapse . subsection(scalability implications) the explicit decomposition of the bound yields clear insights into scalability . on the source side the dependence of indicates that learning with eqcs is polynomial in problem size—substantially more favorable than the exponential blop faced by generic qnns . on the transfer side shows that moderate increases in problem size close to incur only mild penalties whereas large jumps produce more pronounced degradation . this suggests that a curriculum in which models are trained incrementally on growing is more effective than attempting a single leap from very small to very large instances . subsection(design principles for transferable qrl) beyond asymptotic considerations the bound highlights several principles for constructing transferable qrl agents . first transfer is most reliable when source and target sizes are close since both penalty terms vanish as . second enforcing equivariance is crucial it ensures that the learned policy remains insensitive to permutations of city labels and that the architecture scales consistently with problem size . third regularization of parameter magnitudes during training can reduce generator mismatch directly lowering the leading term of . finally the assumption of smooth task families such as uniformly random euclidean tsps underpins the validity of the structural term . for distributions exhibiting abrupt combinatorial transitions transfer penalties may be underestimated underscoring the importance of choosing problem families with stable local statistics when seeking transferability . subsection(symmetry and data assumptions) the effectiveness of crosize transfer ultimately hinges on symmetry preservation and data assumptions . the tsp is invariant under permutations of city labels inducing symmetry for any -city instance . our qnns are designed to be -equivariant at training time and by scaling the generators appropriately -equivariant at deployment . this architectural consistency ensures that symmetrreserving inductive biases are retained during transfer . if equivariance were broken—for example by embedding an -qubit circuit into a larger system without adapting generators—the penalty could grow without bound. distributional assumptions also play a critical role . whereas prior generalization results are framed in supervised learning with i.i.d. samples qrl operates in a sequential setting with notationary trajectories . we assume that training on -city tsps involves sufficient exploration and episodes to approximate the optimal value function well . the symmetrreserving design of eqcs helps avoid barren plateaus and provides a rich hypothesis space making this assumption reasonable . when deployed on larger -city tasks the shared symmetry ensures that learned strategies remain semantically relevant with performance loss captured precisely by . subsection(transfer feasibility) the derived bound thus provides a quantitative roadmap for scalable quantum reinforcement learning. if grows polynomially—as our analysis indicates—then zerhot transfer is feasible across modest size differences while finuning can recover performance for larger gaps . in contrast if transfer costs grow sharply with even equivariant circuits would be limited to neaized transfers . our results therefore motivate a practical strategy train eqased policies on moderately large instances and extend to larger ones incrementally within the range where remains controlled. this balance between transfer cost and transfer feasibility underpins the scalability of qrl for combinatorial optimization . section(incorporating the theoretical performance degradation bound) label(app peregradation) to strengthen the connection between the theoretical analysis and the of statector simulation) the empirical validation in this work was performed using statector simulation . in this framework the full quantum state of an -qubit system is represented explicitly as a vector of complex amplitudes . the application of a quantum gate is modeled as the multiplication of this vector by a unitary matrix . the computational complexity of this approach scales exponentially with begin(itemize) item memory complexity item time complexity per gate for local gates and up to for the global eqc gates end(itemize) this exponential scaling introduces a hard ceiling on problem sizes that can be simulated in practice . even with stathrt supercomputers statector simulation becomes infeasible for systems larger than roughly 40 qubits a threshold often referred to as the classical supremacy barrier . as such extending empirical analysis of equivariant quantum circuits eqcs to problem instances of realistic size e.g. for tsp is beyond reach using this methodology alone . subsection(a more scalable alternative tensor network simulation) a natural direction for overcoming this limitation is the use of tensor network methods specifically the emph(matrix product state mps) representation together with emph(matrix product operators mpos) for implementing gates . unlike the statector approach which stores the entire exponentiaize wavefunction an mps represents an -qubit state as a sequence of interconnected tensors of bounded rank . the storage requirement of an mps is mathcal(o)m cdot d cdot chi^2 where for qubits and is the bond dimension a hyperparameter that controls the entanglement captured across any bipartition of the qubit chain . for states with limited entanglement can remain small and constant enabling simulation of systems with hundreds or even thousands of qubits with memory that scales only linearly in . this approach is the cornerstone of modern computational physics for strongly correlated onimensional quantum systems . subsection(challenges with global gates and the role of mpos) a key challenge in applying mps simulation to eqcs is handling the global entangling gates characteristic of the architecture . naively the application of a global unitary such as u e^(-i theta h) qquad h sum (j1)^m o j where each is a local pauli operator would cause the bond dimension to grow exponentially eliminating the efficiency advantage . however an important structural property of such generators makes them particularly suitable for mpased simulation . operators expressed as sums of local terms admit efficient mpo representations . in fact even for a global operator such as the mpo bond dimension required is exactly independent of system size . this observation provides a pathway to simulate eqcs efficiently using tensor networks since the global gates central to the model can be encoded compactly as mpos . subsection(workflow for tensoetwork simulation) the anticipated simulation strategy for eqcs on largcale tsp instances would proceed as follows begin(enumerate) item state initialization . the initial product state e.g. is prepared as an mps with bond dimension . a maximum allowable bond dimension is set to control the accuracfficiency tradff . item mpo construction . for each eqc layer with unitary the generator is represented as an mpo of constant bond dimension . item gate application . the unitary is applied to the mps using one of several standard approaches begin(itemize) item emph(trotteuzuki decomposition ) approximate applying local exponentials sequentially with temporary bond growth . item emph(timvolving block decimation tebd ) apply shorime evolutions using mpos followed by truncation . item emph(direct mpo approximation ) approximate itself as an mpo with small bond dimension and apply directly . end(itemize) item bonimension truncation . after each gate the mps bond dimension increases . the state is truncated back to using singular value decomposition svd discarding small singular values and introducing a controlled approximation error . item iteration . repeat steps for all circuit layers . item measurement . observables also represented as mpos are computed from the final mps efficiently . end(enumerate) subsection(complexity comparison) the shift from statector simulation to mps/mpo simulation changes address the challenge of generalization in quantum reinforcement learning qrl for combinatorial optimization focusing on the traveling salesman problem tsp . training quantum policies on large tsp instances is often infeasible so existing qrl approaches are limited to smalcale problems . to mitigate this we employed equivariant quantum circuits eqcs that respect the permutation symmetry of the tsp graph . this symmetrware ansatz enabled zerhot transfer of trained parameters from city training instances to larger ity problems . building on recent theory showing that equivariant architectures avoid barren plateaus and generalize well we derived novel generalization bounds for the transfer setting . our analysis introduces a term quantifying the structural dissimilarity between and node tsps yielding an upper bound on performance loss under transfer . empirically we trained eqased policies on small city tsps and evaluated them on larger instances finding that they retained strong performance zerhot and further improved with finuning consistent with classical observations of positive transfer between scales . these results demonstrate that embedding permutation symmetry into quantum models yields scalable qrl solutions for combinatorial tasks highlighting the crucial role of equivariance in transferable quantum learning . end(abstract) section(introduction) combinatorial optimization co problems such as the traveling salesman problem tsp lie at the heart of numerous reaorld applications in logistics network routing and circuit design . these problems are typically nard meaning their computational complexity grows rapidly with instance size rendering exact solutions intractable for large inputs . as such co serves as a natural testbed for developing and evaluating scalable optimization techniques . recent advances in machine learning particularly emph(reinforcement learning) rl have shown promise in tackling co problems by learning heuristic strategies from data . in parallel emph(quantum reinforcement learning) qrl has emerged as a hybrid paradigm that uses quantum circuits to represent and optimize policies or value functions . qrl holds the potential to exploit quantum parallelism for more expressive or compact policy representations . however a major challenge remains most qrl methods must be retrained from scratch for every new problem instance or size . this limits their practicality and scalability especially for applications requiring generalization across varying problem sizes . in this work we propose a new approach to enhance transferability in qrl by leveraging emph(equivariant quantum circuits) eqcs . these are structured quantum neural networks that preserve the symmetry of the problem domain specifically permutation invariance over city indices in tsp . this architectural inductive bias ensures that the policy output transforms consistently under input permutations naturally aligning with the structure of symmetric co problems . let theta n denote the optimized parameters learned on tsp instances with n cities . we ask the following question begin(tcolorbox)colbackgray!5!white colframeblack!80!black titleresearch question can parameters theta n trained on small tsp instances be transferred to larger tsp instances with m > n using the same eqc architecture without retraining ? end(tcolorbox) the motivation stems from the observation that eqcs like their classical permutatioquivariant counterparts can maintain architectural consistency across input sizes . this raises the possibility that a policy trained on small instances may encode structural insights that generalize across scales analogous to transfer learning in classical ml . prior work in quantum optimization such as has also shown that fixearameter quantum algorithms like qaoa can generalize well across problem sizes suggesting that sizgnostic inductive priors can be effective in quantum settings . the theoretical findings and outlines directions for future research in scalable quantum learning . section(foundations and related work) label(sec background) this work is motivated by three principles central to combinatorial optimization and learning theory emph(symmetry) emph(locality) and emph(generalization). these principles guide our use of equivariant quantum circuits eqcs in scalable quantum reinforcement learning qrl . below we review their role and the associated literature . subsection(symmetry) permutation symmetry is inherent in the traveling salesman problem tsp relabeling cities does not alter the tour length or solution structure . equivariant quantum circuits eqcs central to our methodology embed this property by design . eqcs enforce a structural bias that compels learned policies to depend only on relational features such as graph topology and inteity distances rather than absolute city indices . when tsp instances are drawn from the same distribution e.g . cities sampled uniformly from the unit square larger problems represent natural statistical extensions of smaller ones . consequently an eqc trained on smaller instances can internalize generic heuristics such as prioritizing local proximity or avoiding long jumps early in a tourthat remain effective as instance size grows . this role is analogous to classical graph neural networks gnns which are welstablished in their ability to generalize across graphs of varying sizes when tasks exhibit permutation symmetry . prior work by skolik et al . demonstrated that a shallow dept eqc trained on 2ity tsps generalized effectively to unseen instances of the same size outperforming qaoa and surpassing noquivariant circuits that failed to scale . our work builds directly on these findings by extending the analysis to emph(crosize transfer) where parameters trained on -city instances are applied to larger -city problems . subsection(locality) locality provides a second crucial inductive bias for scalability . classic heuristics such as the neareseighbor method christofides’ algorithm and insertioased approaches all rely on locally greedy decisions constructing tours incrementally based on immediate neighborhood information . this property underpins their ability to scale to larger instances without global recomputation . in machine learning several studies reinforce the centrality of locality . ouyang et al . showed that rl agents trained on 5ity tsps generalized effectively to instances with up to 1000 cities when using permutatioquivariant architectures . fu et al . introduced a compositional framework where small pretrained gnns are recursively applied to larger tsps . in contrast joshi et al . demonstrated that rl solvers trained only on trivially small problems fail completely on larger instances highlighting the need for inductive biases such as permutation symmetry and locality . more recently zhang and li showed that rl agents relying only on local neighborhood information still produce neaptimal tours for large graphs . together these findings suggest that if eqcs can encode localitware heuristics their learned strategies should naturally persist across instance sizes . subsection(generalization) generalization links symmetry and locality into a coherent framework for scalable learning . under standard assumptions including independent uniform sampling of cities adherence to the triangle inequality and the dominance of short edges in optimal tours policies trained on small tsps should maintain their effectiveness when transferred to larger ones . euclidean tsps are known to exhibit scalnvariant local structure and classical results such as the beardwooaltoammersley theorem imply that optimal tour length grows smoothly as . this supports the idea of emph(graceful performance degradation) where approximation error increases slowly with instance size and can be mitigated through limited finuning rather than full retraining . in quantum models generalization is intertwined with trainability . quantum neural networks often encounter barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially with system size . a tradff also arises between expressivity and generalization overly expressive circuits risk overfitting while highly constrained circuits lack flexibility . symmetrased designs offer a way forward . schatzki et al . proved that permutatioquivariant qnns avoid barren plateaus by restricting optimization to symmetronsistent subspaces while mernyei et al . empirically confirmed stable scaling with depth and qubit count . from a quantum information perspective adding qubits to a local eqc primarily affects redundant degrees of freedom while global entangling gates such as u gmathcal(e) gamma explefti gamma sum (ij in mathcal(e) z i z jright distribute parameter influence uniformly across edges . this phenomenon echoes parameter concentration observed in qaoa further suggesting robustness to scale . collectively these insights support our central hypothesis eqcs trained on small tsp instances encode transferable instancndependent structural information . symmetry ensures consistency across permutations locality provides scalnvariant heuristics and the absence of barren plateaus ensures that finuning is efficient . together these principles make scalable quantum optimization via crosize transfer both theoretically plausible and empirically promising . section(theoretical framework for zerhot transfer) label(sec theory) subsection(background and motivation) a significant practical hurdle in applying qrl much like its classical counterpart is the ofteubstantial computational cost associated with training an agent from scratch for every new problem instance or scale . transfer learning particularly zerhot transfer offers a compelling strategy to mitigate this issue . in this paradigm a model trained on a source task is applied directly to a new related target task without any further training on the target tasks data . for tsp this could mean training a qrl agent on an ity problem and then deploying it to solve an ity problem ideally with . the ability to effectively transfer learned knowledge would drastically improve the scalability and utility of qrl approaches . subsection(problem statement) this work addresses the specific scenario of zerhot transfer learning in the context of qrl for the tsp . a qrl agent whose policy or value function is parameterized by a quantum neural network qnn is first trained to find optimal or neaptimal solutions for an -city tsp . the parameters obtained from this training phase are then directly applied to an -city tsp where . the central objective of this work is to derive a theoretical bound on the expected performance of this transferred qrl agent when evaluated on the larger -city problem instances . subsection(approach and contribution) the theoretical derivation presented in this work will be grounded in the principles and mathematical framework of theorem 4 from schatzki et al . 2024 . this theorem provides generalization guarantees for gap between the -city and -city tsp tasks which arises from the change in problem scale and structure . end(itemize) the derivation of such a bound is essential for understanding the fundamental maintained during transfer . this involves a careful adaptation of a generalization bound which concerns performance on unseen data from the same task distribution to a transfer learning bound which concerns performance on a different though related target task distribution . a key challenge and focus will be the introduction and characterization of a task dissimilarity metric that bridges this conceptual gap . subsection(notation and preliminaries) label(sec notation) the following lists the key notation that will be used in this paper begin(itemize) item true performance of the qrl agent subsection(theoretical performance degradation) to connect theory with experiments we operationalize the transfer penalty by estimating its constants and overlaying the theoretical lower bound on the empirical plots . this shows that zerhot performance consistently lies above the predicted bound while finuning rapidly closes the gap . the full derivation of the constants estimation methodology and validation figures are provided in appendix . <caption start> empirical validation of the theoretical transfer performance bound . each panel shows the performance of a model trained on a source tsp of the equivariant policies blue circles consistently remains above the predicted theoretical lower bound red dashed line and the empirical results never enter the theoretically excluded region . this provides strong evidence for the correctness of the derived bound . at the same time the plots reveal the inherent difficulty of zerhot transfer performance degrades as the gap between the source size and target size grows a trend qualitatively captured by the bound . this underscores the limitations of directly applying a policy trained on smaller instances to significantly larger problems without adaptation . critically finuning emerges as a highly effective strategy . the finuned models green squares achieve substantially better performance than their zerhot counterparts demonstrating that the transferred equivariant policy serves as an excellent initialization in parameter space. with only minimal additional training on the target task the model rapidly adapts to larger problem instances . this validates our core contribution a theoretically grounded transfer methodology whose practical utility is realized through efficient finuning. section(conclusion and future directions) label(sec discussion) this study demonstrates that embedding permutation symmetry into quantum reinforcement learning agents enables knowledge learned on small tsp instances to transfer effectively to larger ones . the theoretical bound we derived explains this transferability in terms of generalization and a transfer penalty while our empirical results confirm that such equivariant policies not only generalize zerhot but also serve as powerful initializations when finuned . we now conclude with some reflection on its significance and future works . subsection(significance and limitations) the derived bound provides several significant theoretical insights begin(itemize) item it offers a formal framework for analyzing zerhot transfer in the context of equivariant qml models extending singlask generalization guarantees . item it explicitly identifies the key factors that influence transfer performance particularly the interplay between source task learning quality and the inherent difficulty of transferring across different problem scales . item it underscores the importance of symmetry -equivariance not only for efficient learning on a single task but also as a potentially beneficial structural prior for transfer learning as it ensures the model respects fundamental problem invariances across different scales . end(itemize) however the analysis also has limitations begin(itemize) item the precise functional form and magnitude of the constants within the transfer penalty term remain abstract . a more concrete firsrinciple derivation of would require a significantly deeper dive into the geometric properties of the qnn parameter landscapes and the specific dynamics of the qrl agent which is beyond the scope of this work. item the bound relies on a specific set of assumptions regarding the qrl agent tsp encoding and the transfer mechanism . deviations from these assumptions e.g. different qnn adaptation strategies or tsps with fundamentally different structures at different scales could lead to different performance characteristics . item the analysis is purely theoretical and does not account for practical hardware noise or imperfections in implementing the qnn which also notes an area for future work for their singlask results . end(itemize) subsection(future research directions) this work opens several avenues for future research begin(itemize) item textbf(refining ) a primary goal would be to develop a more rigorous and detailed mathematical characterization of the transfer penalty . this could involve tools from optimal transport information theory or by analyzing the sensitivity of the qnn’s output to changes in its underlying equivariant generators when parameters are fixed. incorporating more specific structural properties of tsp instances e.g. from random matrix theory or geometric graph theory could also yield tighter bounds . item investigating alternative transfer mechanisms the current work assumes direct parameter transfer with adaptation of generator forms . future research could explore begin(itemize) item finuning a subset of layers of the -adapted qnn using a small amount of -city data fehot transfer . item layeise transfer strategies where earlier layers potentially capturing more general features are transferred and later layers are rnitialized or finuned. item methods for transforming or adapting the parameters themselves to better suit the -city problem perhaps guided by the change in to . end(itemize) item impact of noise extending the analysis to include the effects of quantum hardware noise on the generalization error in the source task and on the transfer penalty is crucial for assessing practical applicability on neaerm quantum devices . item broader applicability while we focused on tsp the approach of adapting theorem 1 and introducing a transfer penalty term could potentially be applied to other hard combinatorial optimization problems with underlying permutation symmetries such as quadratic assignment problem flowship scheduling problem where equivariant qrl agents can be trained and generalization bounds applied similarly . end(itemize) in conclusionthe theoretical bound derived in this paper provides a foundational step towards understanding the capabilities and limitations of zerhot transfer for equivariant qrl agents . it emphasizes that while symmetry offers powerful advantages for learning the challenges of transferring knowledge across different problem scales are norivial and warrant careful theoretical and empirical investigation . newpage newpage input(appendix) end(document)

computing and information sciences florida international university miami fl email (iyengar)@cs.fiu.edu) ) begin(abstract) quantum circuits can be reduced through optimization to better fit the constraints of quantum hardware . one such method initiatate dependent optimization isdo reduces gate count by leveraging knowledge of the input quantum states . surprisingly we found that isdo is broadly applicable to the downstream circuits produced by circuit cutting . circuit cutting also requires measuring upstream qubits and has some flexibility of selection observables to do reconstruction . therefore we propose a statependent optimization sdo framework that incorporates isdo our newly proposed measurtate dependent optimization msdo and a biased observable selection strategy . building on the strengths of the sdo framework and recognizing the scalability challenges of circuit cutting we propose noeparate circuit cutting—a more flexible approach that enables optimizing gates without fully separating them . we validate our methods on noisy simulations of qaoa qft and bv circuits . results show that our approach consistently mitigates noise and improves overall circuit performance demonstrating its promise for enhancing quantum algorithm execution on neaerm hardware . end(abstract) ieeepeerreviewmaketitle section(introduction) quantum circuit optimization focuses on generating more efficient and streamlined circuits to improve circuit fidelity . one such quantum circuit optimization approach is initiatate dependent optimizations isdo which leverages knowledge of the quantum input states to eliminate or modify gates without altering the circuits output . however isdo is limited in its applicability to the front few layers of the circuit . in this work we show that isdo is ideally suited to circuit cutting which enables the simulation of large quantum circuits on smaller devices . circuit cutting primarily relies on wire cutting measuring upstream qubits in various observables and preparing downstream qubits in various initial states . this process splits the original circuit into upstream and downstream subcircuits each of which is smaller than the uncut circuit . we find that existing isdo can often be applied to downstream subcircuits to improve output fidelity . for upstream subcircuits we introduce measure‐state dependent optimization msdo which mirrors isdo but applies optimization at the measurement stage . observing that different subcircuits exhibit varying fidelities we introduce a biased observable selection strategy to choose those subcircuits that yield higher fidelity in wire‐cutting reconstruction . we then integrate downstream isdo upstream msdo and biased observable selection into a unified state‐dependent optimization sdo framework—a circuit optimization scheme specifically tailored for wire cutting . an overview of circuit cutting with the sdo framework is shown in figure . cutting its applicability is limited because the number of subcircuits grows exponentially with the number of cuts . to address this situation we extend circuit cutting to noeparate circuit cutting cutting) circuit cutting allows us to execute a large circuit by running smaller more manageable subcircuits . to perform circuit cutting three steps must be completed . first we identify cut locations along the circuit’s wires ; making cuts at these points decomposes the circuit into independent fragments . for example the circuit shown on the rightmost side of figure can be cut on the second qubit marked by a red cross splitting it into two separate fragments . second at each cut location the upstream wire is measured in a chosen set of observables and the downstream wire is initialized in the corresponding eigenstates . consequently each fragment must be executed multiple times ; we refer to each circuit that needs to be executed as a subcircuit . a commonly used basis is the pauli set mathcal(b) (i x y z). more precisely wire cutting decomposes a singlubit density matrix rho as in this decomposition each term mathbf(tr)mrhom represents measuring the upstream wire exponentially with the number of cuts . several works have proposed methods to mitigate these overheads . subsection(initiatate dependent optimization ) label(subsec initiatate dependent optimization) title(a survey of methods for mitigating barren plateaus for parameterized quantum circuits) begin(abstract) barren plateaus are a formidable challenge for hybrid quantulassical algorithms that lead to flat plateaus in the loss function landscape making it difficult to take advantage of the expressive power of parameterized quantum circuits with gradienased methods . like in classical neural network models parameterized quantum circuits suffer the same vanishing gradient issue due to large parameter spaces with noonvex landscapes . in this review we present an overview of the different genesis for barren plateaus mathematical formalisms of common themes around barren plateaus and dives into gradients . the central objective is to provide a conceptual perspective between classical and quantum interpretations of vanishing gradients as well as dive into techniques involving cost functions entanglement and initialization strategies to mitigate barren plateaus . addressing barren plateaus paves the way towards feasibility of many classically intractable applications for quantum simulation optimization chemistry and quantum machine learning . end(abstract) section(introduction) indent variational quantum algorithms vqas are an emerging hybrid classiuantum technique in which a trial wave function is constructed as a function of parameterized unitary gates to minimize some objective function via an observable . these algorithms use quantum subroutines where measurement statistics are evaluated with classical processing to update the circuit parameters of the trial wave function with an iterative optimization loop . in all a vqa consists of an initial state and parameterized unitaries that model circuit structure a problepecific cost function that encodes the optimization problem and training procedure for parameter updating . these optimization algorithms are akin to finding the lowest expectation energy ground state which serves as a model for many domains of interest including quantum simulation condensed matter physics quantum chemistry combinatorial optimization and machine learning . as current quantum devices are incapable of robust erroorrection on long sequences of gate operations vqas serve as a neaerm bridge for bencarking real world applications on nisq devices by taking advantage of classical computation to mitigate noise and coherence times on current devices . understanding the structure and adaptive nature of vqas to handle the constraints of neaerm quantum computers is integral to achieving faulolerance in the lonun the optimization framework for parameterized quantum circuitspqcs used in vqas hold many parallels to variational techniques from classical machine learning for neural networks where gradient methods are used in the context of optimization problems to minimize noinear functions . in supervised learning models for classical neural networks a goal of optimization is to learn the weights of node mappings between layers using derivative based cost functions to calculate the loss between parameter updates . it is an open area of research to identify suitable quantum problems where complex correlation between data is classically hard and leads to better model expressibility over classical neural networks as deep learning models can have on the order of 100 billions of parameters leading to costly training schemes . though pqcs and quantum neural networks are used interchangeably in literature quantum neural networks are an application of pqcs which leverage a quantutate encoding function and classical optimization loop . newline however both pqcs and neural networks suffer from vanishing gradients due to the increasing complexity of the parameter space . this phenomenon is known as a barren plateau in quantum literature and is one of the most prevalent challenges for achieving scalability for variational quantum algorithms . as our system size increases the loss landscape becomes increasingly noonvex and makes it harder to find an optimal parameter set for our objective function rendering gradienased optimization unusable in the context of the exponential dimensionality of the hilbert space . various factors lead to the emergence of barren plateaus in pqcs including include global cost functions haar random parameter initialization unstructured ansatz information scrambling noise and highly entangled circuits . if the issue of barren plateaus can be circumvented in pqcs then classically intractable components of variational problems may be subsection(vanishing gradient versus barren plateaus) label(sec vanishinarren) the analog of the barren plateau phenomenon as described in def . in classical machine learning literature is the vanishing gradient for deep neural networks . however the fundamental distinction for a pqc lies in the inherent impossibility of accessing the quantum state at intermediate stages during computation . while it is conceivable to employ measurements of ancillary quantum variables for the extraction of partial information any attempt to observe the entire state of the system would inevitably perturb its quantum properties . consequently the execution of a variational circuit cannot be analogously equated with the forward pass of a neural network . furthermore the development of a circuit learning algorithm closely mirroring backpropagation becomes a formidable challenge due to the necessity of preserving the intermediate state of the network throughout computation. first we will formalize the definition of backpropagation to then draw a distinction between vanishing gradients and barren plateaus . newline in both a neural network model and our pqc model the parameter update function for chain in eq . is what gives rise to vanishing gradients through the backpropogation process in deep learning ; the gradient for a weight in a neuron depends on the sum of all the paths connecting that neuron to the output . when there are many layers the error from activation functions are magnified leading to large effects for earlier layers leading to a exponential decrease in the gradient . on the contrary large prediction errors lead to exploding gradients where the magnitude of the gradient is large and thus never converges . fine tuning methods are needed to modulate the impact of this multiplicative factor. subsubsection(barren plateaus) vanishing gradient arose from a dynamic process of error propagation that could be controlled with modifications the activation function or parameter initialization ; barren plateaus on the otheand have no means of occurring through a dynamic process such as backpropogation in a pqc as there is no way to access intermediate information of a circuit . we have discussed various cases of barren plateaus in the quantum case in sec . that were largely related to the circuit design sec . degree of expressibilitysec . and the circuit parameterization landscapesec .  thus a barren plateau can be regarded as a static phenomenon that appears everywhere in a circuit that is a consequence of the circuit ansatz features more closely
