18795 japan ) affiliation advanced ict research institute national institute of information and communications technology 58 iwaoka nishi kobe 65492 japan ) date(today begin(abstract) we evaluated a multolor twhoton entangled state generated in silicon via spontaneous fouave mixing sfwm as a potential source for bosonic integrated circuits . spatially entangled photon states were created using a pair of silicon waveguides that produced signal and idler photons through sfwm allowing us to observe quantum interference between them . assuming that the frequencies of the multolor photons were nearly identical we characterized the generated quantum state by performing quantum state tomography on the bosonic system using a linear optical circuit . this study demonstrates the feasibility of using photoair sources generated in silicon via sfwm in bosonic optical circuits and highlights their potential for a wide range of applications in silicoased optical quantum technologies . end(abstract) section(introduction) silicoased optical integrated circuits are promising platforms for largcale quantum information processing . their advantages include excellent scalability and controllability as well as low optical loss in the telecommunications wavelength band . optical interferometers fabricated on silicon substrates offer compact and stable architectures allowing for the integration of multiple stages to construct programmable linear optical circuits . importantly photon pairs generated via spontaneous fouave mixing sfwm in silicon serve as a valuable quantum resource as both the photon source and the circuit can be monolithically integrated on a single silicon chip . although the distinct frequencies of the signal and idler photons produced by sfwm typically inhibit quantum interference it is still possible to observe interference by creating spatial or temporal superpositions of photon pairs from multiple sfwm sources . this approach has enabled various experimental demonstrations including timin entanglement the generation of largcale quantum states and the realization of a twubit quantum processor . in typical experiments where photon pairs are generated via sfwm in silicon the frequency separation between the signal and idler photons is much smaller than their absolute optical frequencies . under these conditions linear optical components such as multode interference mmi couplers and phase shifters fabricated in silicon waveguides behave almost identically for both the signal and idler photons . as a result their frequencies can be effectively regarded as nearly identical . this frequency indistinguishability constrains the dimensionality in which linear optical circuits can manipulate the quantum states generated by sfwm limiting it to a subspace of the maximum possible hilbert space . therefore it is essential to understand the degree of controllability that a linear optical circuit can exert over a given quantum state . such understanding not only guides the reduction of required optical components for practical quantum information processing but also facilitates accurate evaluation of the generated quantum states . in this manuscript we revisit the hilbert space associated with quantum states generated via sfwm and manipulated through linear optics exploring the potential of sfwenerated photons as a source for bosonic quantum circuits . specifically we show that quantum states produced in a linear optical circuit with two spatial modes can be mapped onto a bosonic system described by a twode samolor twhoton state which is mathematically equivalent to a spi system . experimentally we generated entangled photon pairs in a silicon waveguide using an interferometric sfwm source and injected them into a macehnder interferometer mzi integrated on the same chip . by varying the phase of the interferometer we observed higisibility interference fringes in the twhoton output confirming the coherent superposition of spatiaode nooike states . to quantitatively characterize the generated quantum states we performed quantum state tomography within the spi framework of the twode twhoton hilbert space . the quantum state was reconstructed by measuring the expectation values of spi operators along five independent directions enabling the evaluation of the states purity coherence and internal consistency . these results demonstrate that silicon photonic integrated circuits combined with spiased analysis and ohip linear optics provide a practical and scalable platform for implementing and characterizing bosonic quantum circuits . section(quantum state generated via sfwm in a linear optical circuit) figure illustrates a twode linear optical circuit that includes an interferometer with a variable phase shifter . the input state consists of two photons—a signal photon and an idler photon—generated via noegenerate spontaneous fouave mixing in silicon . as a result integrated circuit . by exploiting the neaegeneracy of signal and idler photon frequencies we treated the generated state as a bosonic twhoton system and manipulated it using ohip linear optics . higisibility quantum interference fringes were observed and the state was quantitatively evaluated through spi-based quantum state tomography . the experimentally reconstructed density matrix showed high purity and internal consistency with only a few percent deviation in the verification of spin operator relations . these results validate the use of spiased tomography for bosonic states and demonstrate the precision and stability achievable in silicon photonic platforms . our findings confirm that photoair sources based on sfwm in silicon combined with ohip linear optical circuits provide a scalable and accurate platform for implementing bosonic quantum circuits . this architecture holds promise for advancing integrated quantum photonic technologies particularly for 45136731 iran) date(today) begin(abstract) monitored quantum circuits offer great perspectives for exploring the interplay of quantum information and complex quantum dynamics . these systems could realize the extensiveltudied entanglement and purification phase transitions as well as a rich variety of symmetrrotected and ordered noquilibrium phases . the central question regarding such phases is whether they survive in reaorld devices exhibiting unavoidable symmetrreaking noise . we study the fate of the symmetrrotected absorbing state and chargharpening transitions in the presence of symmetrreaking noise and establish that the net effect of noise results in coherent and incoherent symmetrreaking effects . the coherent contribution removes a sharp distinction between different phases and renders phase transitions to crossovers . nevertheless states far away from the original phase boundaries retain their essential character . in fact corrective feedback in adaptive quantum circuits and postselected measurements in symmetric chargonserving quantum circuits can suppress the effects of noise thereby stabilizing the absorbing and chargharp phases respectively . despite the unavoidable noise in current quantum hardwares our findings offer an optimistic outlook for observing symmetrrotected phases in currently available noisy intermediatcale quantum nisq devices . moreover our work suggests a symmetrased benchmarking method as an alternative for characterizing noise and evaluating average local gate fidelity.end(abstract) section(introduction) understanding the relationship between quantum dynamics and information flow in complex faroquilibrium manody systems has become a major theme in contemporary research . in particular the interplay of unitary evolution which drives entanglement growth and information scrambling and emph(nonitary) monitoring by local measurements which suppresses entanglement proliferation has stimulated a flurry of recent activity . this interplay has given rise to an entirely new paradigm characterized by the fascinating phenomena known as emph(measuremennduced phase transitions) mipts . a compelling approach to enhance the observability of mipts involves guiding the dynamics of a quantum system through the implementation of additional feedback gates conditioned on measurement outcomes . a typical example of this approach is the employment of interactive feedbacks based on measurement results to direct the system towards emph(absorbing states) which typically exhibit symmetry breaking of a global symmetry . moreover a wide variety of predicted phases and phenomena arising from the monitored dynamics such as the chargharpening transition rely on the presence of specific symmetries of the unitaries . however the impact of symmetrreaking which is inevitable in real quantum hardware remains largely unexplored . <caption start>label(fig1<caption end> in this work we address the effects of symmetrreaking single qubit gates noise two types of monitored quantum circuits i adaptive circuits with corrective feedback that steers the system toward an ordered absorbing state fig.; and ii nodaptive -symmetric monitored circuits which lack feedback but utilize charge conserving unitaries . errors in the execution of quantum gates are a major source of noise in current digital quantum simulators and vast efforts have been devoted to quantum error correction and error mitigation techniques . these random errors which do not respect symmetries of the circuit pose a particular challenge for symmetrrotected phenomena . moreover due to the irreproducible nature of noise across different runs of the same circuit the ensemble resulting from multiple state preparations no longer represents a pure state but rather a statistical mixture . our key finding is that the net effect of symmetrreaking noise gives rise to coherent and incoherent symmetrreaking contributions . the coherent contribution can be regarded as an additional symmetrreaking contribution to the symmetrreserving unitary gates thus removing the strict distinction of symmetrrotected phases and transforming the phase boundaries into crossovers . despite this states far away from the original phase boundaries retain their essential nature even in the presence of strong symmetrreaking noise . this enables observation of weaklodified absorbing states and sharp charge states at higher monitoring rates . in adaptive circuits the higher monitoring rate is relatively cosree as the absorbing state transition does not require postselection . however the higher monitoring rate to observe a charge sharpening in -symmetric quantum circuits comes with a higher postselection overhead . section(results) eventually become fully suppressed as we approach the chargharp phase . emph(color(blue) chargharpening with noise) . similar to the effect in adaptive circuits noise explicitly breaks the symmetry of entanglement and the associated measuremennduced phase transition has been studied extensively . there have also been theoretical proposals to protect the entanglement phase transition from decoherence noise using schemes that apply quantunhanced operations . in this scheme instead of performing projective measurements quantum information is transferred and stored in a quantum memory for posrocessing by a quantum computer . in this work we have addressed the symmetrreaking role of noise on absorbintate and sharpening transitions in adaptive and symmetric quantum circuits . our numerical results show that the noise induced by generic singlubit errors only deteriorates the absorbintate and chargharp phases at low and intermediate measurement rates . however we find that at sufficiently high measurement rates the destructive effect of noise even at maximal error rates can be suppressed thus retrieving the absorbintate and chargharp phases . the underlying reasons for the noise resilience and rstablishment of these phases in the two considered types of circuits are not exactly the same . in adaptive circuits the feedback mechanism following miircuit measurements helps to cancel the noise effects . in contrast in symmetric circuits where there is no corrective feedback postselecting over the measurement outcomes is the key tool in combating noise . another striking finding is that a generic singlubit gate error bounded by a maximum angle results in partially coherent noise . the coherent contribution determined by the average angle qualitatively alters the dynamics revealing a fully quantum character . this is in sharp contrast to noiseless case where the quantum channel describing the averaged effects of measurement and unitary gates is found to be effectively classical . as a result of inherent nolassicality in the presence of noise the system exhibits a crossover rather than a sharp transition between the fuzzy and ordered chargharpened or absorbing phases . quantum circuits with feedback are currently available in various quantum computing architectures . there is no major bottleneck for achieving noise resilience in adaptive circuits even with existing nisq hardware . however postselection with an exponential execution overhead is only feasible for small circuits with qubits . given that there have already been various attempts and proposals to bypass the postselection problem in noisree circuits an interesting problem to explore is finding alternative efficient methods that do not require full postselection but still enable the observation of chargharpening transitions even in noisy settings . based on the availability of feedback mechanisms in existing quantum hardware not only can our results be directly tested but this approach may also offer potential side applications in noise characterization . in the standard method known as emph(randomized benchmarking) techniques the error rates and fidelities of quantum gates are typically characterized by applying long sequences of randomly sampled gates often from the clifford group . based on our findings we propose an alternative approach that leverages the relationship between the error amplitude or gate fidelity and the average value of the absorbintate order parameter in adaptive circuits . this connection allows us to estimate the average gate fidelity of an otherwise symmetric circuit by measuring the steadalue of an order parameter avoiding the need for complex gate sequences . this method for characterizing the average gate fidelity can provide sufficient information about error rates averaged over all of the qubits in scenarios where we are primarily interested in qubiveraged quantities such as in quantum simulations . this approach is a practical alternative to conventional randomized benchmarking when the focus is on systeide averages rather than individual qubit performance . section(methods) in our numerical calculations we first consider a sufficiently large set of individual trajectory dynamics that involve the application of twubit unitary gates random measurement processes and in the case of adaptive circuits additional corrective singlubit unitaries following the measurements . for each trajectory the noisree part of the unitaries is sampled uniformly from a symmetronstrained random haar set of twubit operators . the measurement sites are randomly chosen with a probability at each time step and the outcomes of each singlubit measurement are drawn from a twtate distribution based on the born probabilities of the states and . the noise terms are implemented according to their description in the main text by randomly selecting a set of qubits and applying a random rotation with angle and a rotation axis . for each run and at each time instance any number of qubits between zero and can be chosen resulting in an average of noisy qubits in the limit of large system sizes and long times . after executing each trajectory i.e . each circuit execution we construct a density matrix from the final states according to eqs . and for adaptive and -charge conserving cases respectively . in the -charge conserving case poselection of measurement outcomes is necessary . without poselection the combination of noise and random measurement outcomes would result in a completely mixed state . therefore poselection is essential to diagnose the chargharp state and assess purification when noise is present . in this setting we construct the density matrix for each sequence of measurement outcomes separately . the primary difference between the implementation of adaptive versus -symmetric circuits aside from the form of the unitaries and the presence/absence of feedback is that in the -symmetric case the average over measurement outcomes is taken after obtaining the density matrix for a given sequence of outcomes as described in eq .  this corresponds to poselecting on measurement outcomes in experiments . for smaller circuits we numerically evaluate the application of the unitaries in a brickwork structure as well as the measurements and noise terms on the multubit state using our python code . for larger circuits where the measurement rate is sufficiently high as in the results shown in fig . we use the package pastaq for mpased calculations . the analytical results continuouime dynamics of a manody hamiltonian by implementing discrete trotter steps of duration . however when is sufficiently large the discrete dynamics exhibit qualitative differences compared to the original evolution potentially displaying novel features and manody effects . we study an interesting example of this phenomenon by considering the integrable trotterization of a prototypical integrable model the xxz heisenberg spin chain . we focus on the welnown bipartition protocol where two halves of a large system are prepared in different macrostates and suddenly joined together yielding norivial nonequilibrium dynamics . building upon recent results and adapting the generalized hydrodynamics ghd of integrable models we develop an exact largcale description of an explicit onimensional quantuircuit setting where the input left and right qubits are initialized in two distinct product states . we explore the phenomenology predicted by the ghd equations which depend on the trotter step and the gate parameters . in some phases of the parameter space we show that the quantuircuit largcale dynamics is qualitatively different compared to the continuouime evolution . in particular we find that a single microscopic defect at the junction such as the addition of a single qubit may change the nonequilibrium macrostate appearing at late time . ) vspace(baselineskip) vspace( tiform t) noindentrule(textwidth)( tiform t) tableofcontents noindentrule(textwidth)( tiform t) vspace( tiform t) 	section(introduction) label(sec intro) the trotteuzuki decomposition is at the basis of the idea of quantum simulation . up to a controlled error this decomposition allows us to break down the continuouime evolution of a manody system into a series of elementary twody interactions of duration which could be implemented as emph(quantum gates) in a quantum circuit . the trotter time controls the accuracy and determines the number of gates applied . unfortunately external noise limits the number of operations which can be carried out in the noisntermediatcale quantum nisq devices available today . therefore since simulating the continuouime dynamics typically requires application of many quantum gates fulledged quantum simulation remains a norivial challenge . motivated by this picture the past few years have witnessed growing interest in genuinely discrete dynamics where the trotter time is not small . the reason behind this interest is twold . on the one hand these models may be easier to implement in current quantum platforms since a norivial evolution may be observed over a small number of trotter steps . on the other hand discrete dynamics may exhibit qualitative differences compared to the original hamiltonian system with novel phenomena and manody effects . for typical hamiltonians recent work has shown that increasing indefinitely the trotter time leads to a sharp transition see also when is increased beyond a threshold value approximation errors become uncontrolled at large times . as a consequence the evolution becomes chaotic and one expects the rapid onset of locaquilibrium infinitemperature physics . this mechanism however is not ubiquitous and a different behavior is expected for instance in the presence of integrability where extensively many local conservation laws prevents the onset of quantum chaos . <caption start>sketch of the bipartition protocol . the system is initialized by joining at the origin two product states the figure corresponds to the néel and antéel states and evolved by applying a homogeneous quantum circuit trotterizing the integrable xxz continuouime dynamics is the duration of the trotter step . a lightcone spreads ballistically from the junction inside of which norivial dynamics takes place . we study the profiles of local observables arising at late times . the plot shows the example of the staggered spinmagnetization and is obtained by solving the ghd equations cf . sec .  in the past few years they have received significant attention due to their dynamical features their rich underlying mathematical structures and seminal work demonstrating experimental implementation in current quantum devices . prominently ref . has shown the existence of trotter transitions in integrable quantum circuits manifesting in the correlations of the salled generalized gibbs ensemble gge . as gges describe the latime physics of integrable systems this result is interesting as it implies that the information on the discretized structure of the dynamics is not washed out at coarsrained time scales . in this work we build upon the results of ref . which focused on homogeneous translationvariant settings and investigate the physics of integrable quantum circuits in more general noquilibrium situations . we focus in particular on the prototypical model of the xxz heisenberg spin chain and consider the simplest case where the system is prepared in an inhomogeneous state namely the salled bipartition protocol . the latter consists in a special type of emph(quantum quench) where the two halves of a system are prepared in distinct macrostates and subsequently left to evolve according to the system unitary dynamics cf . fig .  while conceptually simple this problem is hard . for integrable systems its understanding has required significant theoretical work over the past decade culminating in the development of the salled generalized hydrodynamics ghd a very versatile and powerful theory . in the bipartition protocol the ghd predicts that local subsystems at a given distance from the junction equilibrate to local stationary states depending only on the ratio defining a reference frame moving away from the origin . such stationary states are characterized by spacependent gges which are quantitatively determined by a solution to the hydrodynamic equations . the latter depend on the features of the specific model considered including its particle content and symmetries . for this reason while ghd provides a very general framework the qualitative features of the dynamics can vary greatly from model to model leading to a series of works aimed at exploring the phenomenology of the biparition protocol in different integrable systems . the goal of this work is to apply the ghd framework to study the bipartition protocol in the xxz integrable quantum circuit . based on the known spectral properties of the model we first derive the ghd equations and study their dependence on the trotter step and circuit parameters . we consider an explicit protocol where the input left and right qubits are initialized in two distinct product states and evolved by applying a homogeneous quantum circuit . we find that the qualitative features of the discrete dynamics may vary greatly from the continuouime evolution . most prominently we show that a single microscopic defect at the junction such as the addition of a single qubit may change the nonequilibrium macrostate appearing at late time . our work complements ref . further exploring the interesting dynamical features of integrable quantum circuits in manody settings . the rest of this work is organized as follows . we begin in sec . introducing the xxz quantum circuit and its bethe ansatz solution . in sec . we discuss the bipartition protocol and derive the necessary technical ingredients for its analytic description . they include obtaining the gges corresponding to different initial states generalizing the results of ref . and deriving the ghd equations for integrable quantum circuits . our results are discussed in detail in sec . where we provide predictions for the system dynamics at different points in the parameter space by numerically solving the ghd equations . our conclusions are presented in sec . while the appendices contain the most technical aspects of our work . section(the model) label(sec the model) subsection(the formalism . while initially developed for the study of integrable hamiltonians the tba can be straightforwardly extended to the quantuircuit setting . in essence the tba formalism is based on the string hypothesis which postulates how the solutions to the bethe equations organize themselves in the complex plane in the limit with the density kept fixed . in particular the string hypothesis states that the rapidities organize themselves into sets of elements forming a string of length which is interpreted as a bound state of quasiparticles . each string features a center which is the bountate quasimomentum . therefore we can associate to each macrostate a set of functions in a large system of size yields the number of -quasiparticle bound states with rapidities in the interval . in order to achieve a complete thermodynamic description the tba formalism also introduces the set of hole distribution functions for the -string centers denoted by . the hole distribution functions are analogous to the distribution of vacancies i.e . unoccupied states in the ideal fermi gas at finite temperature . the precise form of the rapidity and hole distribution functions depends once again on the phase of the model . we therefore separate the discussion between the two cases in the following . before proceeding it is important to mention that the validity of the string hypothesis has been verified in a number of cases including the present quantuircuit setting where the resulting predictions have been tested numerically against independent tensoetwork computations . initial states) for systems with traditional hamiltonian dynamics most of previous work on bipartition protocols have focused on the setting where two halves of the system are prepared in different equilibrium states . typically the latter are chosen as finitemperature states with different temperatures or chemical potentials . in this case when the two halves are joined together the norivial dynamics only takes place in a region increasing linearly in time and centered around the junction . alternatively one could consider preparing two halves of the system in noquilibrium states with a simple structure . as discussed in sec . each half of the system far enough from the junction is then expected to relax to a stationary gge which depends on the initial state . accordingly at late time the norivial dynamics again takes place only in a region increasing linearly in time and centered around the junction . in the quantuircuit setting under consideration the hamiltonian is not conserved by the discrete time evolution and the corresponding gibbs states are not equilibrium states . therefore the most natural choice is to initialize the two halves of the system into different nonequilibrium states which we choose as product states . this setting is natural in light of benchmark implementation in quantum devices since product states are the easiest to be prepared in digital platforms . our analysis relies on the possibility to characterize the gge associated to the chosen initial states . as shown in ref . this problem can be solved for a large family of states called integrable generalizing the constructions of the hamiltonian case . the family of integrable states includes all twite shifnvariant product states allowing us to study a wide class of bipartition shows the profiles of the local magnetization and the corresponding current . we see that the profiles are flat outside the lightcone which is an expected feature indeed corresponds to the maximum velocity at which quasarticles propagate . taking reference frames moving at a velocity with larger absolute value the system is described by the gges associated by the initial left/right states . the magnetization is vanishing at but the profiles is norivial inside of the lightcone signaling the emergence of norivial noquilibrium steady states . we also note that the magnetization and current profiles display no points of nonaliticities inside of the lightcone . this is expected since at the nonteracting points we have a single quasarticle string type . the features described above are qualitatively similar to what one could have expected based on the ghd in the xxz heisenberg model . yet away from the limit of small trotter step one may expect the emergence of qualitative differences compared to the continuouime evolution . we can see that this is indeed the case even at the nonteracting point of the model with noero . to this end we consider the bipartition protocol where the left and right states are prepared in a néel and antéel state respectively . note that the resulting initial state can be thought of as a homogeneous néel state in which a defect in the form of a qubit is added in the center of the chain . begin(figure*) 	includegraphicsscale0.9(neelneelpi3 2.pdf) 	caption(late time profiles after the bipartition protocol in which the left and right models in which all charges satisfy singlite translation symmetry such as the xxz heisenberg chain both states equilibrate to the same gge . accordingly after an initial transient time there would be no norivial dynamics at large spacime scales . this is intuitive when viewing the initial state as created by the addition of a single defect in an homogeneous configuration . indeed a local initial perturbation does not typically lead to a change in the macroscopic state of the system although exceptions exist see e.g on the other hand the trotterized xxz circuit is invariant under translation by two sites which allows for the possibility that the néel and antéel states give rise to different gges . it is worth mentioning that one could construct local integrable hamiltonians breaking the singlite translation symmetry but preserving twite shift invariance for which a similar behavior is observed . however while this construction would appear rather emph(ad hoc) in the continuouime limit here it appears naturally as a consequence of increasing the trotter step . the ability to change the global latime behavior by a single defect in a circuit setting is also of obvious interest for benchmark experiments in current digital devices . indeed approximating the continuouime evolution of a twite shifnvariant hamiltonian would require implementing very deep circuits even to reach short times which is unfeasible on current devices . instead existing experiments have already shown that integrable circuits can be implemented keeping sufficient coherence over a number of discrete steps that is enough to appreciate the emergence of latime features . fig.b shows our quantitative results for this bipartition protocol in the nonteracting case . the profiles of the local magnetization and current demonstrate the emergence of norivial dynamics even at macroscopic scales . interestingly we see that there is an accumulation of the magnetization charge inside of the lightcone with the current changing sign at the left and right ends . this does not violate the global conservation of the -magnetization in the system as the excess charge propagates to infinity . it is natural to ask whether this peculiar behaviour is a special property of the nonteracting points . we see in the next section that this is not the case and that norivial dynamics in this bipartition protocol survives the presence of interactions . subsection(observable profiles at the interacting points) we finally present our results for different bipartition protocols at generic points of the parameter space . first it is important to state that for the initial states considered the magnetization and current profiles are trivial in the gapped regime . this is because both the néel and dimer states have vanishing magnetization and in the gapped regime there are no additional charges breaking the spilip symmetry . we have numerically verified this prediction by solving the ghd equations and computing the magnetization and current profiles . in all cases we have found that the profiles of these observables are flat up to the chosen numerical accuracy . note that the solutions to the ghd equations for the néeimer bipartition protocol do have a norivial dependence on even in the gapped regime . conversely the gges associated with the néel and antéel states coincide and there is no norivial dynamics taking place in the corresponding bipartition protocol . next we move on to discuss the gapless phase . in fig . we study the protocol where the left and right states are initialized in the dimer and néel states respectively . we plot the profiles of the staggered and averaged magnetization respectively both showing norivial dynamics . compared to the nonteracting circuit we see additional points inside of the lightcone where the profiles are not smooth . similarly to the ghd profiles in the xxz heisenberg chain these points are associated to the maximum velocities of distinct quasarticle types namely of strings with increasing length . we also see that both observables display noonotonic and highly irregular profiles . while the figure shows data for one value of and we have verified that qualitatively similar features arise for different choices of the circuit parameters . finally we discuss the bipartition protocol where the two halves of the system are prepared in the néel and antéel state respectively . we report an example of our results in fig. where we plot the profiles of the staggered and averaged magnetization and the current again in the gapless phase . as anticipated all plots show norivial profiles and once again we see nonalyticity points inside of the lightcone although they are less evident than in the néeimer bipartition protocol . as in the nonteracting case we see that the dynamics causes an accumulation of magnetization at the origin fig.b with the current taking opposite values at the left and right ends of the lightcone . section(outlook) label(sec outlook) in this work we have developed and studied the ghd of integrable quantum circuits . our main finding is that for generic choices of the circuit parameters the largcale dynamics displays qualitative differences compared to the continuouime evolution of the corresponding xxz hamiltonian . in particular considering quenches from product states we predict peculiar features which can be detected by looking at the latime dynamics of simple observables such as the local magnetization . our work opens several directions for future research . first it would be important to provide predictions for more general observables and correlations than those considered in this work . technically this problem requires the derivation of new formulas for the expectation value of local observables in stationary states described by a given rapidity distribution function . while this is a hard problem we expect that one could generalize the results available for the hamiltonian model extending the computation presented in ref . for the simplest case of onoint functions . along similar lines it would be interesting to also consider the entanglement dynamics in integrable quantum circuits . in the hamiltonian setting building upon the results for the evolution of bipartite entanglement in homogeneous systems recent work has shown how the ghd formalism is naturally suited to describe the entanglement dynamics in inhomogeneous setting . we expect that the results of refs . apply directly to integrable quantum circuits potentially allowing us to investigate the role of discrete spacime in the largcale dynamics of bipartite entanglement . finally it would be important to analyze the feasibility of observing some of the features predicted by our work in benchmark experiments in existing quantum platforms . to this end it would be necessary to study how finitize corrections affect our predictions . in addition one would also need to analyze the effect of noise possibly taking into account recent strategies for quantum erroitigation . we leave these interesting questions for future work. section*(acknowledgements) we
